comments.author: CloudyTiger
comments.text:
CloudyTiger (cc_3), assigned this bead by GoldLotus. TWO THINGS: (1) I cannot claim it — the tracker refuses, and (2) the D8 primitive decision is done and mailed; recording it here because Agent Mail is timing out.

BLOCKER ON THE CLAIM, exact text: 'cannot transition frankengit-fg057-crypto-keys-q04 from open to in_progress: repository group capacity verification_debt would exceed its hard limit (current: 36, prospective: 37, hard: 36, counting: leaf_work; policy: workflow.capacity.groups.verification_debt)'. 36 beads sit in verification debt so the tracker is applying backpressure against a 37th. Only GoldLotus can drain it, by closing at a green sweep or raising the cap. fg002b is one of the 36 and is said to close at the next green sweep, so this may clear itself. I have NOT written code under this bead while unclaimed; everything below is reading and a decision, which the bead and GoldLotus both put ahead of code anyway.

D8 PRIMITIVE RECOMMENDATION — reuse everything, implement nothing new. Two reasons.

First, the specification says so three times: threat model section 8 'Fundamental pure-Rust crypto dependencies are preferred over bespoke unreviewed primitive implementation'; plan 35.6 'require explicit review rather than bespoke unreviewed primitives'; D8 'Avoid bespoke primitive design.'

Second, it costs nothing. Every primitive fg057 needs already has an ACTIVE registry row AND is already in Cargo.lock: ed25519-dalek DEP-051, ed25519 DEP-050, signature DEP-127, curve25519-dalek DEP-044 (signatures); aes-gcm DEP-016, chacha20poly1305 DEP-031, aead DEP-014, poly1305 DEP-102, universal-hash DEP-143 (AEAD); hmac DEP-069 (MAC); zeroize DEP-172, subtle DEP-132 (hygiene); getrandom DEP-064, rand_core DEP-112 (randomness). Reuse adds zero new crates and moves Cargo.lock not at all.

WHY I AM NOT REPEATING MY SHA ARGUMENT: I argued in-house for SHA-1/SHA-256 and stand by it, but both reasons were specific and neither transfers. Constitution section 8 assigns object-ID calculation and both repository hash formats to FrankenGit's owned surface and says nothing comparable about signatures, AEAD or MACs; and the section 11.6 collision hook needs per-block chaining values that no general-purpose crate exposes, which has no analogue here. The clean auditable line is: OWNED = the hashes that compute Git object identity; REUSED = everything else. This includes HMAC, the one I could most easily have kept — a 30-line construction over my own SHA-256 with RFC 4231 vectors, which I earlier called 'free'. I am recommending against it: free in dependency terms, not free in consistency terms, and neither exception argument applies.

CONSEQUENCE TO ACCEPT DELIBERATELY: fgit-crypto stops being a zero-dependency crate. I advertised that property in the frozen-surface announcement and it goes away. I think it is the right trade — the property was a means, not the goal — but it is GoldLotus's to accept rather than mine to slip in.

THE REGISTRY DECISION IS NOT 'NOTHING': every one of those rows reads allow_transitive_admitted_runtime with rationale 'asupersync 0.4.9 transitive'. They are admitted BECAUSE THE RUNTIME NEEDS THEM, not because the key layer does. Treating an existing transitive row as authorisation for direct first-party use is exactly the dependency-smuggling shortcut I would flag in someone else's crate. Two shapes: (a) reclassify the ~12 rows to a direct-admission class, or (b) add new rows alongside the transitive ones. I lean (b) — it keeps 'the runtime pulled this in' and 'the identity layer depends on this deliberately' as separate auditable facts, and if asupersync's closure ever drops one, the row justifying my use survives and the failure is loud. Also: DEP-004 pure-rust-crypto still matches nothing real, and this is the moment to make it a real pattern or retire it rather than leave a row that looks like policy and enforces nothing.

THREE OPEN QUESTIONS I WILL NOT ANSWER UNILATERALLY. (1) Randomness is a side effect: key generation needs a CSPRNG, getrandom is admitted, but under the constitution entropy access looks like a capability and effects that acquire responsibility use typed obligations — should key generation take a capability from the Asupersync Cx, or is direct getrandom acceptable in a leaf crate? This changes the API shape; CobaltForest owns the runtime profile and may have a view. (2) KMS/BYOK is an interface point in D8, not an implementation — I plan a trait boundary plus a typed refusal for unsupported providers and no provider implementation in this bead. (3) Cryptographic erasure integrates with fg033's deletion states, which do not exist yet — I plan to own the primitive (destroying key material makes dependent ciphertext typed-unrecoverable, never silently readable) and leave the deletion-state wiring to fg033 as a noted follow-up, which the bead's own 'noted follow-ups' clause allows.

I will not touch registries/dependency_policy.tsv or any manifest until GoldLotus rules. Once ruled, the order is ADR section, then registry rows under reservation, then code.

comments.author: CloudyTiger
comments.text:
Preparatory reading continued while the claim stays blocked (verification_debt still 36/36 as of this check). Two code-point findings that directly shape this bead, both reported to cc_2 on fg002a.

1. SIGNATURE SCHEME CODE POINT 1 IS ALREADY SQUATTED. fgit-codec defines SignatureSchemeId(u16) as an opaque code point with no registry behind it — try_new accepts any nonzero value, which is exactly the gap fg057 fills. Its test fixtures use scheme 1 with signature bytes vec![0xa0; 64]. 64 is precisely the Ed25519 signature length, and 1 is the obvious code point to hand Ed25519. Allocating it would turn those fixtures into well-formed-looking Ed25519 signatures: right scheme, right length, only an actual verification failing. DESIGN CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS BEAD: I will not allocate 1. The signature-scheme registry gets a reserved harness range mirroring the digest one — 0xfff0..=0xffff, exported as a const with a compile-time assertion that no registered scheme lands inside it — and real schemes start from a base that leaves the squatted value alone. This is the second namespace to need that treatment, which suggests reserving a harness range should be the default when defining a code-point registry rather than a reaction.

2. The fgit-codec fixture digests are tagged with production code point 1 (sha1, 20 bytes, git_identity_only per my registry) while carrying 32 bytes, even though that crate already defines CORPUS_ALGORITHM_CODE_POINT = 0xfff1 and uses it elsewhere. Not fg057 work and not mine to fix, but it tells me the pattern recurs whenever fixtures are written before a registry exists, which is the situation fg057 is in right now for signature schemes.

DESIGN NOTES CARRIED FORWARD from reading threat model section 8 and plan 35.6/D8:
- Key purposes are enumerated in the threat model, not invented by me: identity, authority/admin, capsule, evidence, package/release, webhook, tenant encryption, recovery. Eight, closed, and "cross-purpose key use unrepresentable" means type-level separation — the same phantom-parameter technique that makes GitOid<Sha1> and GitOid<Sha256> non-comparable, applied to Key<P: KeyPurpose>.
- AEAD binds tenant, repository, object class, key purpose and version (threat model section 8), so the AAD construction is a domain-separated framing decision of the same kind as the internal-identity preimage, and it should reuse the framing rather than grow a second one.
- A ciphertext copied across incompatible key domains is not a valid placement (plan 12.5/13.7), so key domain has to be part of the type, not a runtime tag checked late.
- Cryptographic erasure is a typed deletion state (19.4): destroying key material makes dependent ciphertext typed-unrecoverable, never silently readable.

DELIVERED: HMAC-SHA-256 (RFC 2104) in src/mac.rs and HKDF-SHA-256 (RFC 5869) in src/derive.rs, both zero-dependency constructions over this crate existing SHA-256.

ON THE D8 QUESTION, and a correction to my own earlier recommendation: I had recommended reuse across the board including HMAC, on consistency grounds. Re-reading the dispatch, GoldLotus already ruled the default — "stay zero-dep and in-house like SHA (HMAC-SHA-256 for MAC)" — and the mail-first requirement applies specifically to AEAD or a signature scheme needing a NEW dependency. So the standing instruction governs and I built HMAC and HKDF in-house. My consistency argument is not withdrawn but it is overruled, and I am noting that rather than quietly acting as if I had won it. AEAD and signatures remain behind the ruling; nothing has been added to any manifest and Cargo.lock has not moved.

WHY THESE TWO ARE NOT BESPOKE PRIMITIVE DESIGN, which the spec forbids three times: HMAC and HKDF are constructions, not primitives. RFC 2104 and RFC 5869 specify them completely in terms of an underlying hash; neither has a key schedule, a nonce, or secret-dependent control flow. The thing the spec is protecting against is inventing a primitive, and this is not that.

WHY HKDF BELONGS IN THIS BEAD: the threat model requires envelope encryption to bind tenant, repository, object class, key purpose and version, and requires a ciphertext copied across incompatible key domains not to be a valid placement. Both are statements about which key a domain gets, which is a derivation problem. The info argument is where the domain separation lives, and it takes the SAME length-prefixed framing as the internal-identity preimage rather than growing a second convention — concatenating domain fields unframed is exactly how two domains end up deriving one key.

EVIDENCE: goldens/mac_vectors.tsv (RFC 4231 TC1-TC7 plus empty-key, exactly-block-width and one-over-block cases) and goldens/derive_vectors.tsv (RFC 5869 A.1-A.3 plus per-domain and maximum-output cases). Every expected value derived with Python hmac/hashlib, an implementation unrelated to the Rust, and the published RFC cases are included so the oracle is itself checked against the standard rather than trusted. Tests in tests/keyed_vectors.rs: rfc_4231_hmac_sha256_known_answer_vectors, streaming_hmac_matches_one_shot_for_every_chunk_width, rfc_5869_hkdf_sha256_known_answer_vectors, one_root_secret_derives_unrelated_keys_per_domain, an_output_longer_than_the_construction_allows_is_refused (paired with the at-ceiling permitted case), tag_verification_accepts_the_true_tag_and_rejects_every_single_bit_forgery (all 256 single-bit forgeries), a_wrong_key_produces_a_different_tag.

TWO NON-CLAIMS, in the module docs and worth reading before relying on this. verify_mac is a data-independent fold behind core::hint::black_box: that is the strongest statement safe Rust supports without a dedicated constant-time crate, it is NOT a measured constant-time guarantee, and it is not proof against a compiler that reasons differently. And key material is NOT zeroized on drop — the compiler may elide such writes and this crate has no zeroize dependency, so a caller holding long-lived key material should assume it stays in memory. Closing that is a dependency decision (zeroize is already admitted transitively as DEP-172), not something to fake with a manual loop that the optimiser deletes.

comments.author: CloudyTiger
comments.text:
Third slice at 781c61c: rotation, revocation, cryptographic erasure, receipts.

THE DESIGN POINT worth stating, because it is where this kind of code usually goes wrong: rotation, revocation and erasure are the same question asked of different epochs — may this epoch ISSUE, versus may it VERIFY — and collapsing those into one boolean is exactly how a revoked key keeps signing. KeyHistory answers them separately. Rotation retires the previous epoch, which still verifies and no longer issues, so data written before the rotation stays readable — that is the bead drill. Revocation stops both AND leaves nothing issuing rather than silently falling back to the retired epoch; the caller must rotate deliberately. Erasure is terminal.

ERASURE IS A STATE, NOT AN ABSENCE. An erased epoch answers MaterialErased and never EpochUnknown. That distinction is the whole of plan 19.4: unknown invites a caller to retry, resynchronise, or diagnose corruption, whereas erased says permanently unrecoverable by design and names the epoch. Recoverability exposes the same fact as a value (Recoverable / WithheldByRevocation / PermanentlyUnrecoverable) so a caller can record it without matching on a refusal. The key commitment survives erasure so the destroyed epoch stays identifiable in evidence rather than becoming a hole.

RECEIPTS: every transition returns a LifecycleReceipt with length-prefixed canonical bytes and a domain-separated identity under NEW REGISTRY ROW 31, frankengit/key-lifecycle-receipt/v1. That means fg033 (deletion states) and fg010 (capsules) can commit revocation and erasure evidence as a body with an identity rather than a log line, which is what the acceptance line about integrating with fg033 needs from my side.

TESTS, tests/key_lifecycle.rs: rotation_keeps_old_epochs_verifying_while_only_the_new_one_issues; rotation_must_advance_and_a_replayed_epoch_is_refused (with the later-epoch permitted twin); revocation_cuts_issuance_and_is_receipted; erasure_is_permanent_and_typed_rather_than_an_unknown_key (asserts MaterialErased is distinct from EpochUnknown, that erasing twice is refused, and that an erased epoch cannot be revoked back into a lesser state); erasing_the_active_epoch_leaves_nothing_issuing; a_receipt_carries_a_verifiable_domain_separated_identity; two_transitions_never_share_a_receipt_identity; histories_of_different_purposes_are_different_types.

TWO NON-CLAIMS, in the module docs. A receipt is CANONICAL, not AUTHENTICATED: nothing signs it because signing is behind the D8 ruling, so it detects alteration by anyone who re-derives it and proves nothing about who issued it. And erasing an epoch removes this process copy and records the state — it cannot reach copies a caller made, backups, or allocator pages not yet reused, so the evidence is a claim about the key registry and not about every byte that ever held the key. Overstating either would be the more damaging error here than understating it.

SEAM DEFECT found while coordinating fg033a with YellowLotus per GoldLotus's instruction (msg 7942).
Recorded here so it survives the sweep even if the mail does not get actioned. Mail 7982 has the full
version.

FINDING: repair reconstructs ciphertext but not keys, so restore can currently "succeed" into
permanently unreadable data.

Verified by inspection, not assumed:
- fgit-chronicle has ZERO reference to key lifecycle. grep for Erased/erasure across
  crates/fgit-chronicle/src/ returns nothing.
- CapsuleDefect (fgit-chronicle/src/verify.rs, landed under fg010b at 37cbd31) has five variants:
  ObjectBodyMissing, SegmentTruncated, SegmentManifestCorrupt, IdentityMismatch, PredecessorStale.
  NONE of them is "the key for this data was erased".

Consequence: a capsule referencing tenant ciphertext whose key epoch was cryptographically erased
either goes undetected or surfaces as ObjectBodyMissing. Under BackupProfile::FullClosureWithRepair
that classifies RecoverableWithRepair, and an operator is invited to reconstruct. The reconstruction
succeeds, produces bytes, and yields data nobody can ever read. Worse: if the erasure was a deletion
obligation being discharged, reconstruction resurrects bytes that were supposed to be gone and the
restore report says it worked. Same shape as the masquerade hazard one layer down -- quiet, and the
system looks healthy.

PROPOSED FIX: a sixth variant, CapsuleDefect::KeyMaterialErased { purpose, epoch }, joining
IdentityMismatch and PredecessorStale on the is_reconstructible() == false side so it forces
FailClosed under every profile including FullClosureWithRepair. The classifier already has the
shape; it is missing the input. an_identity_mismatch_is_never_repairable_under_any_profile is the
test template.

The crypto side should FEED it rather than duplicate it: fgit_crypto::Recoverability already
distinguishes Recoverable / WithheldByRevocation / PermanentlyUnrecoverable and
KeyHistory::recoverability(epoch) answers it. Two vocabularies for "is this key usable" is how a
revoked key gets honoured on one path and refused on another. Revocation and erasure must classify
DIFFERENTLY in restore: revocation withholds material that still exists and is reversible by policy,
erasure destroyed it and is reversible by nothing.

WHY I HAVE NOT LANDED IT: fg010b is batch_pending at 37cbd31 and queued for the sweep. Moving code
under it now would break the revision binding on evidence I already reported. GoldLotus's call:
either fg010b rework after the sweep (I take it) or inside fg033a (YellowLotus takes it, I review).
I have no preference beyond it not being forgotten, because until it exists the classifier will
confidently tell an operator that unreadable data is repairable.

ALSO OPEN, and it is a decision fg033a has to make: keys here are DERIVED from a RootSecret, so
erasing a registry epoch does not erase anything a retained root can recompute -- fg057 asserts this
explicitly in erasure_is_a_registry_decision_and_this_test_says_what_it_does_not_reach. So restore
must decide which model it assumes. Administrative: registry refuses, root survives, restore may
refuse but may NOT claim the data is unreadable. Cryptographic: material stored wrapped and the
wrapping key destroyed, and unreadable becomes true of the bytes. Plan 19.4 wants the second. Nothing
stores wrapped material yet; that is real work and arguably mine rather than fg033a's. Offered.

title: FG-057b: Crypto registry key-abuse, rotation, and erasure campaign
description:
SCOPE (paired evidence campaign for fg057-crypto-keys) — a real trust boundary with no dedicated adversarial coverage today.

The corpus: cross-purpose key-use (a signing key used for envelope encryption must be UNREPRESENTABLE or typed-refused), rotation-window races (old-key data readable through key history; new writes use new key; revocation cuts issuance — all receipted), cryptographic-erasure completeness integrated with fg033 deletion states (destroying keys yields the typed crypto-erased state; residual ciphertext is unreadable), key-domain confusion (ciphertext copied across incompatible key domains is not a valid placement), and downgrade attempts.

ACCEPTANCE

- standard test vectors pass per primitive;

CONSTITUTIONAL CONSTRAINTS (AGENTS.md; non-negotiable)

- Claim lattice (invariant > proof > bounded model > statistical > SLO > benchmark): never describe this work as stronger than its evidence. Record disproven hypotheses in docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE_LEDGER.md + registries/negative_evidence.tsv.
- Run ./scripts/verify.sh fast before and after; stage only intended files; keep generated artifacts out of source.

E2E LOGGING CONVENTIONS (mandatory for every e2e script)
- Scripts live in scripts/e2e/, are bash with `set -euo pipefail`, and source scripts/e2e/lib.sh (built by the e2e-harness bead).
- Every step emits one NDJSON line to the log file AND stderr: {"ts":..., "script":..., "step":..., "cmd":..., "exit":..., "duration_ms":..., "artifact_digests":{...}, "seed":..., "note":...}.
- Assertions log expected vs actual on failure and dump the relevant state directory listing + last 50 log lines of the process under test before exiting nonzero.
- Deterministic seeds are logged and settable via env so any failure replays exactly.
- A final summary line reports steps run/passed/failed and total wall time; exit code is the number of failed steps capped at 1.

      references to object-format / object_format / sha256 ......... 0
      its oracle repository is built with a bare `git init` ......... default SHA-1
      PRESENCE CASE: the same grep finds 25 'advertise' hits in that file, so it reads the

So the project's upload-pack differential lane has never exercised a SHA-256 repository at all. That is not a defect in FG-018c -- its stated scope is the fgit-wire protocol surface, and nothing there promised SHA-256 -- but it does mean this epic cannot inherit SHA-256 differential coverage from it. The coverage has to be built here.

WHY THIS IS NOT RH-9, stated plainly because the shape is adjacent. Follow-up laundering is moving an in-scope acceptance condition into a NEW follow-up in order to close the original. title: fgit-node git-daemon omits object-format=sha256 for SHA-256 repositories
description:
Fresh-eyes read-only review at HEAD 15c8115277205e976036098de5159c3719827ff8.

DEFECT
OneNode supports GitHashAlgorithm::Sha256 through NodeConfig::with_object_format (crates/fgit-node/src/lib.rs:3314-3318), and V1Advertisement emits object-format-specific 64-hex OIDs (it receives repository.object_format at :2958-2963). However the production daemon always parses the fixed capability list at :4007 from GIT_DAEMON_CAPABILITIES, which is exactly agent=frankengit-node at :112. It never advertises object-format=sha256.

FAILING SCENARIO
Configure a OneNode for GitHashAlgorithm::Sha256, provision a non-empty canonical ref, and serve V0 or V1 upload-pack. The first advertised ref carries a 64-hex SHA-256 OID while its NUL capability list contains only agent=frankengit-node. A stock Git client has no hash-domain negotiation signal and retains the SHA-1 default for the advertisement, so it cannot parse/clone the SHA-256 ref correctly. The empty-repository pseudo-ref has the same mismatch: V1Advertisement chooses a 64-zero identity but the daemon supplies no object-format capability.

IMPACT
The node permits a SHA-256 configuration but serves an ambiguous/incompatible git:// advertisement, violating native Git object identity compatibility. The existing direct-domain check at :4717-4745 prevents mixed IDs but does not test the wire capability clients need to select the non-default domain.

EXPECTED FIX/EVIDENCE
Derive daemon capabilities from the authenticated repository object format (including the Git-standard object-format=sha256 capability for SHA-256; preserve the declared SHA-1 profile as applicable). Add V0 and V1 advertisement tests for both non-empty and empty SHA-256 views that assert the capability is present and a pinned-Git differential clone/parse fixture. Pair with a SHA-1 control that preserves its existing negotiated behavior.

NON-CLAIM
No Git/cargo command was run in this read-only review; the scenario follows the direct configuration and advertisement control flow.

comments.text:

The defect, confirmed still live at HEAD 0fbfd0e before I touched anything: the daemon parsed a fixed GIT_DAEMON_CAPABILITIES list for every session, so a SHA-256 repository advertised 64-hex OIDs with no object-format capability and a stock client kept the SHA-1 default.

  git_daemon_capabilities(object_format) derives the list at the ONE production
  construction site (the other three Capabilities:: uses in the file are
  Capabilities::default() inside the test module).
  SHA-256 -> agent=frankengit-node object-format=sha256
  SHA-1   -> agent=frankengit-node   (byte-identical to before)
  The value comes from GitHashAlgorithm::as_str(), not a hardcoded string, and the
  match is exhaustive so a future object format is a compile error rather than a
  silently unadvertised domain.

  SHA-1 IS DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED. A client that sees no object-format selects sha1
  anyway, so a redundant token would alter every existing SHA-1 advertisement for no
  compatibility gain. If the owner wants object-format=sha1 emitted explicitly, that is
  a one-line change to the match arm and I have no objection -- I chose the reading that
  matches "preserve the declared SHA-1 profile as applicable".

TESTS

  git_daemon_capabilities_advertise_the_object_format_only_for_sha256
      exact bytes for BOTH formats, plus both lists parsed through the same
      Capabilities::parse_v1 the daemon feeds them to -- a string comparison alone would
      not prove they are wire-valid. Includes the permitted twin (SHA-1 must NOT gain the
      capability).
  one_node_advertises_object_format_sha256_for_its_empty_sha256_repository

  one_node_advertises_object_format_sha256_on_protocol_v1_as_well_as_v0
      same, for protocol v1: exact bytes including the "version 1" prelude packet. The

MUTATION-VERIFIED, not merely passing. Reverting the call site to the fixed const (cargo check first, restored byte-identical, cargo check green after):

    one_node_advertises_object_format_sha256_for_its_empty_sha256_repository  FAILED
    git_daemon_capabilities_advertise_the_object_format_only_for_sha256       ok
    one_node_serves_its_authenticated_empty_repository_without_a_fixture_pack ok

  Exactly the right test kills it. The other two correctly survive, and that is itself
  worth recording: THE UNIT TEST ALONE WOULD NOT CATCH A REWIRED CALL SITE, and the
  pre-existing SHA-1 test is unaffected, which shows the SHA-1 path is genuinely
  independent rather than incidentally passing.

Gate: RCH_CARGO_WRAPPER_BYPASS=1 cargo check -p fgit-node --all-targets, exit 0, "Checking fgit-node" present. Filtered test run: 3 passed, 0 failed (54 filtered out); then 2 passed after adding the v1 case. I did not run the full --all-targets suite for this crate -- prior experience in this wave is that long fgit-node test runs are culled mid-run -- so this is a filtered result and I am labelling it as one.

  1. NON-EMPTY SHA-256 view advertisement tests. The crate's test module has no
     loose-object fixture infrastructure at all (no objects/ layout, no zlib, no

comments.author: ChartreuseHorizon
comments.text:
DIFFERENTIAL MEASUREMENT AGAINST PINNED GIT 2.54.0 -- AND IT CONTRADICTS MY OWN SHA-1 DECISION. ChartreuseHorizon. Run through the sandboxed oracle (scripts/e2e/oracle/oracle.sh, pin git-2.54.0, Bubblewrap-isolated), never a bare upstream invocation, per section 3.1.

WHAT UPSTREAM ACTUALLY ADVERTISES for an empty repository, both formats:

  --object-format=sha1
    0100 0000000000000000000000000000000000000000 capabilities^{}\0multi_ack thin-pack
    side-band side-band-64k ofs-delta shallow deepen-since deepen-not deepen-relative
    no-progress include-tag multi_ack_detailed no-done object-format=sha1 agent=git/2.54.0-Linux

  --object-format=sha256
    011a 0000...0000 (64 zeros) capabilities^{}\0... no-done object-format=sha256
    agent=git/2.54.0-Linux

GIT ADVERTISES object-format FOR **BOTH** FORMATS, INCLUDING SHA-1. My implementation deliberately omits it for SHA-1, and I documented that choice in the code and in my delivery report as "a client that sees no object-format selects sha1 anyway, so a redundant token would change every existing SHA-1 advertisement for no compatibility gain."

That reasoning is COMPATIBLE but it is not what Git does. Section 6 says preserve native Git object identity exactly and makes refusal/advertisement behaviour compatibility semantics, so a deliberate divergence from upstream's own advertisement is a decision that should be declared rather than assumed -- which is exactly what I did assume. The differential lane existed to catch this and it did, on its first measurement.

TWO SEPARATE DIVERGENCES, and only the first is a decision:

  1. PRESENCE. Upstream emits object-format=sha1 for SHA-1 repositories; we emit nothing.
     Changing this is a one-line edit to the match arm in git_daemon_capabilities. It WOULD
     change the expected bytes of the pre-existing test
     one_node_serves_its_authenticated_empty_repository_without_a_fixture_pack, which currently
     asserts b"...capabilities^{}\0agent=frankengit-node\n" exactly. Editing a pre-existing
     golden is the kind of change that must be a deliberate owner decision with evidence behind
     it, not something I do quietly -- RH-3 is specifically about regenerating goldens to force
     green, and I do not want this mistaken for that even though the direction here is the
     opposite (making the assertion stricter and more Git-like).

  2. ORDER. Upstream puts object-format= BEFORE agent=; we emit agent= first. Capabilities are an
     unordered set to a parser, so this is not a functional divergence, but a BYTE differential
     lane would classify it as one. Worth a declared accepted-divergence rather than a surprise.

WHAT I AM NOT CHANGING WITHOUT A RULING. I have not touched the SHA-1 path. The measurement says my documented rationale was weaker than I presented it, and the owner should decide whether to match upstream exactly (emit object-format for both, update the pre-existing golden) or keep the current minimal-divergence profile with this measurement recorded as the justification. Either is defensible now that the evidence exists; what is not defensible is the version where the choice rests on my assumption.

NON-CLAIM. This is an oracle measurement of upstream's ADVERTISEMENT for empty repositories in both formats. It is not a clone/parse differential against our daemon -- see the separate blocker comment about the CLI having no way to configure a SHA-256 node -- and it says nothing about non-empty advertisements or about protocol v2.

comments.author: ChartreuseHorizon
comments.text:
DIFFERENTIAL RECEIPT EXTENDED TO BOTH FORMATS AND BOTH PROTOCOLS, per BoldMoose's ruling. All four measured through the sandboxed oracle (pin git-2.54.0, Bubblewrap, never a bare upstream invocation). ChartreuseHorizon.

PROTOCOL V0/V1 -- capabilities are a space-separated list in the NUL section of the first ref line:

  sha1     ... include-tag multi_ack_detailed no-done object-format=sha1   agent=git/2.54.0-Linux
  sha256   ... include-tag multi_ack_detailed no-done object-format=sha256 agent=git/2.54.0-Linux

PROTOCOL V2 -- each capability is its own pkt-line (v2 reached through the same git-alias trick the
FG-018c suite uses, since the sandbox clears the environment):

  sha1                          sha256
    000e version 2                000e version 2
    001b agent=git/2.54.0-Linux   001b agent=git/2.54.0-Linux
    0013 ls-refs=unborn           0013 ls-refs=unborn
    0020 fetch=shallow wait-for-done
    0012 server-option            0012 server-option
    0017 object-format=sha1       0019 object-format=sha256
    0000                          0000

TWO FINDINGS, and the second one matters for the instruction I was given.

1. PRESENCE IS UNIVERSAL. object-format is advertised for BOTH formats in BOTH protocols. There is
   no configuration in which upstream omits it. That settles the presence question beyond the empty
   sha1/sha256 pair I measured earlier -- it was not an artifact of the empty case.

2. ORDER IS PROTOCOL-DEPENDENT, and the two protocols disagree:
     v0/v1   object-format comes BEFORE agent
     v2      agent comes FIRST and object-format LAST

   So "emit object-format=sha1 ordered before agent=" is correct FOR V0/V1, which is the protocol
   our git-daemon speaks -- the instruction matches the evidence for the surface it applies to. But
   the ordering is not a global Git convention, and anyone who later extends this node to v2 must
   NOT carry the v0/v1 order across. Recording that here so the next reader does not generalise a
   rule that upstream itself does not follow.

WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT DISCHARGE. It discharges "extend the differential receipt to both
formats/protocols where available": all four cells are measured against the pinned oracle. It does
NOT discharge the live clone/parse fixture, which remains blocked on a real owned bootstrap surface
for SHA-256 -- BoldMoose has routed that missing production capability to GoldLotus and has ruled
out a test-only launch path, which I agree with: a test-only launcher would be a fixture standing in
for a capability.

NOT YET APPLIED TO THE CODE. The SHA-1 arm change and the v0/v1 exact-byte expectation updates are
authorised (BoldMoose, msgs 5114/5120, explicitly classified as an evidence-backed compatibility
correction rather than RH-3) but NOT written: BoldMoose needed crates/fgit-node/src/lib.rs for the
r9e0 deadline rework and I released my reservation at 06:08:19Z rather than hold a peer off a batch
failure. I will re-reserve and land it when they are done. My tree was clean at release; all three
of my commits are in.

title: FG-059: Repository incarnations, rename/delete lifecycle, and migration protocol
description:
GOAL
The identity lifecycle machinery of plan 11.1 and 37.5: typed repository incarnations (delete/recreate under the same owner/name creates a NEW incarnation; nothing stale can revive the prior one), rename/transfer flows, logical-vs-physical deletion states surfaced to users (19.4), and backend/namespace migration as a capsule/authority protocol — never "move the home cell".

WHY / BACKGROUND
Incarnation confusion is a real attack/bug class: stale tokens, caches, federation events, webhooks, or object-location records pointing at a deleted-then-recreated name must NOT act on the new repository. Every canonical record already binds the incarnation ID (fg002 schemas); this bead builds the lifecycle: creation mints an incarnation, deletion tombstones it through retention/grace machinery (fg033), recreation mints a fresh one, and all resolution paths (API, transports, webhooks, caches) check incarnation match. Migration (37.5): repository moves between backends/deployments via export-capsule + restore + conditional routing publication — the routing flip is itself a coordinated decision with anti-rollback, and the source enters a typed read-only-then-tombstone sequence.

ACCEPTANCE
- stale-reference corpus: pre-deletion tokens/webhooks/caches against a recreated name all refuse typed (incarnation mismatch);
- rename keeps incarnation (aliases recorded); transfer across owners keeps incarnation with an audit event;
- migration drill: export, restore to a second deployment, routing flip, source freeze — client-observable cutover is atomic (old name serves until flip, then redirects/refuses per policy);
- deletion states surfaced distinctly (hidden / tombstoned-in-grace / authorized / deleted-hot / expired-everywhere / crypto-erased);
- large-scale profile: bounded resumable partitioned export, parallel verified copy, incremental decision catch-up, admission backpressure, exact source/target closure reconciliation, explicit read-only cutover and rollback horizon, with no dual-writable interval or name/incarnation retargeting;
- cohort/organization migration preserves per-repository authority and reports cross-repository progress/partial failure honestly rather than claiming unavailable atomicity.

CODE-UNIT/FAULT TESTS: lifecycle and resolver properties; stale-incarnation planted negatives; migration state-machine/retry/idempotency; bounded chunk/parallelism; duplicate/missing/reordered batches; cutover/rollback; cancellation/restart and source/target corruption.

LIVE E2E: scripts/e2e/incarnation_migration.sh covers delete/recreate plus one repository; scripts/e2e/migration_scale.sh covers a predeclared corpus/byte/ref/forge-event scale, throttling, kill/restart, incremental catch-up, cutover, reconciliation, rollback-before-horizon, and resource tails. Both appear exactly once in the exact suite manifest. Shared-library NDJSON records source/toolchain/profile/source-target deployment and authority identities, repository/incarnation/batch/checkpoint IDs, seed/failpoint, bytes/objects/events copied and verified, expected/actual phase, RPO/downtime/resource tails, artifact/log digests, and replay command; failed state is retained.

CONSTITUTIONAL CONSTRAINTS (AGENTS.md; non-negotiable)
- Pure Rust, edition 2024, dated-nightly pin from rust-toolchain.toml; every first-party crate carries #![forbid(unsafe_code)]; no C/C++ FFI, no C Git/libgit2/JGit/Dulwich/gix, no hidden subprocess fallback. Upstream Git binaries are pinned, sandboxed differential ORACLES only (never production).
- Asupersync is the sole async runtime (no Tokio/async-std/smol). Long-lived work owns children via regions; cancellation is request -> drain -> finalize; effects use typed obligations (Reserved -> Committed -> Acknowledged, or Reserved -> Aborted).
- Closed dependency universe: every crate (incl. transitive, enforced via Cargo.lock scan) must match an active allow row in registries/dependency_policy.tsv. No build scripts/proc macros without a constitutional exception. No network during builds.
- Final-abstraction slices only: no empty crates, no HashMap-pretending-to-be-storage, no fixture-only parser wired as production API. A subset is fine when its unsupported surface is a typed refusal.
- Claim lattice (invariant > proof > bounded model > statistical > SLO > benchmark): never describe this work as stronger than its evidence. Record disproven hypotheses in docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE_LEDGER.md + registries/negative_evidence.tsv.
- Run ./scripts/verify.sh fast before and after; stage only intended files; keep generated artifacts out of source.

title: FG-062: Resolve the license model (decision D14 — launch-blocking)
description:
GOAL
Resolve plan decision D14: the genuine open-source core/client/protocol vs hosted-commercial differentiation structure, replacing the current source-available rider — BEFORE the first implementation release, as docs/LICENSING_DECISION.md already requires.

WHY / BACKGROUND
The current LICENSE is MIT text plus a rider restriction, and every doc consistently says source-available, NOT OSI open source; risk R18 and definition-of-done item 18 make an honest resolution launch-blocking: the final licensing must be genuinely compatible with any public open-source claim, and the current rider must never be marketed as OSI. This is the repository owner's decision — the bead's job is to force the timing (before first code release), assemble the option analysis (core license candidates, contributor agreement implications, hosted-differentiation models per plan 39.8: hosted value is scale/operations/compliance/support, not a correctness fork), and land the outcome consistently across LICENSE, README, LICENSING_DECISION, Cargo metadata, and the claims machinery.

ACCEPTANCE
- decision recorded in docs/LICENSING_DECISION.md with rationale and the exact texts;
- LICENSE, README licensing sections, CONTRIBUTING, Cargo license metadata, and any generated status all consistent on day one of the change;
- if the decision is deferred at any release point, the release refuses (this mirrors the doc's launch-blocking language — wire it into the fg035 release checklist);
- no doc anywhere claims open source until the license actually is.

TEST PLAN: consistency greps wired into the docs lane (licensing-claim phrase checks extended if needed); release-checklist integration fixture in fg035's contract tests.

CONSTITUTIONAL CONSTRAINTS (AGENTS.md; non-negotiable)
- Pure Rust, edition 2024, dated-nightly pin from rust-toolchain.toml; every first-party crate carries #![forbid(unsafe_code)]; no C/C++ FFI, no C Git/libgit2/JGit/Dulwich/gix, no hidden subprocess fallback. Upstream Git binaries are pinned, sandboxed differential ORACLES only (never production).
- Asupersync is the sole async runtime (no Tokio/async-std/smol). Long-lived work owns children via regions; cancellation is request -> drain -> finalize; effects use typed obligations (Reserved -> Committed -> Acknowledged, or Reserved -> Aborted).
- Closed dependency universe: every crate (incl. transitive, enforced via Cargo.lock scan) must match an active allow row in registries/dependency_policy.tsv. No build scripts/proc macros without a constitutional exception. No network during builds.
- Final-abstraction slices only: no empty crates, no HashMap-pretending-to-be-storage, no fixture-only parser wired as production API. A subset is fine when its unsupported surface is a typed refusal.
- Claim lattice (invariant > proof > bounded model > statistical > SLO > benchmark): never describe this work as stronger than its evidence. Record disproven hypotheses in docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE_LEDGER.md + registries/negative_evidence.tsv.
- Run ./scripts/verify.sh fast before and after; stage only intended files; keep generated artifacts out of source.

  The launch-blocking rule LOOKED enforced and was not. `scripts/verify.sh release` refuses today,
  so a reader concludes the gate works. It refuses via refuse_dormant "No releasable FrankenGit
  binary ... exists yet" — a TEMPORARY refusal that FG-035/FG-091 delete the day releases become
  real. The licensing requirement was riding on an unrelated refusal that is scheduled for removal,
  and would have silently evaporated at exactly the moment it started to matter. It had never been
  tested because nothing has ever tried to release. That is the defect this bead closes.

WHAT LANDED AT 6097535:
  - docs/LICENSING_DECISION.md: one canonical machine-readable marker
    <!-- fgit-license-decision: UNRESOLVED -->, a table of every surface that must change in the SAME
    commit when the decision lands, and the reason deferral is enforced rather than remembered. The
    existing option analysis (A-E), decision criteria and provisional wording rule are untouched — I
    added machinery, I did not rewrite anyone's analysis.
  - scripts/license_gate.sh: standalone typed gate. Exit 3 while UNRESOLVED; exit 3 when a recorded
    decision is not stated identically across LICENSE, README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md and root

    from prose, because a gate that guesses is a gate that can be argued with. Standalone on purpose

EVERY REFUSAL PAIRED WITH ITS PERMITTED CASE. A gate only ever observed saying no might be saying no
unconditionally, so the suite builds a resolved, fully consistent surface in a scratch tree and
requires exit 0 from it — then corrupts ONE surface at a time from that same passing tree and
requires each to be caught. Isolating it that way means a failure cannot be blamed on the fixture.

ACT VERSUS MENTION, handled deliberately. The premature-open-source check matches ASSERTION SHAPES
("FrankenGit is open source", an OSI badge), never the bare token. This repository has hit that bug
class four times, including an ADR checker that flagged the very ADR describing the rule. The

CURRENT STATE OF THE DOCS, measured rather than assumed: no document asserts open-source status
today. I grepped for assertion shapes across all tracked Markdown and the four hits are all

NOT DONE, and not smuggled into a follow-up:

  - CONTRIBUTING.md has no inbound contributor terms. The decision document's own required-process
    item 3 demands them before third-party code is accepted, and they depend on the outbound model,

comments.author: JadeFalcon
comments.text:
FG-062 CONTINUATION at 88a29a6 — the open-source claim check stopped enforcing the moment a decision
landed. Third self-audit defect in this gate. STILL BLOCKED on the repository owner's D14 ruling.

THE DEFECT, and why it is the worst of the three. The bead's acceptance says "no doc anywhere claims
open source until the license actually is." My scan was gated on the decision being UNRESOLVED, so
recording ANY decision switched it off — including option E (Business Source / Functional Source),
which is explicitly NOT open source and is exactly the outcome where a stray "FrankenGit is open
source" line does the most damage. The rule outlives the decision; my implementation of it did not.
It would have stopped watching at the moment it most needed to watch, silently, reporting a pass.

THE FIX: record the answer, do not infer it. Second canonical marker
<!-- fgit-license-osi: yes|no -->, `unknown` while D14 is unresolved, required to be exactly yes or
no in the commit that records the decision. The claim scan runs unless it says yes.

WHY RECORDED RATHER THAN DERIVED FROM THE SPDX STRING: deriving it would make this gate maintain its
own copy of the OSI licence list — a second source of truth on a question that has an owner. Options
A/B/C/D make it yes; option E makes it no, and under no the repository keeps saying source-available
for as long as the restriction period runs.

PAIRED BRANCH COVERAGE, the three differing only in the marker: the scan RUNS for a non-OSI
resolution, RUNS while unresolved, STANDS DOWN for an OSI-approved one. Plus the gate refuses a
recorded decision that never answers the question — silence is not "no".

MY OWN FIXTURES CAUGHT IT FIRST, which I want on the record because it is the useful kind of
evidence: three PERMITTED cases went red immediately, because their scratch decision documents
carried no OSI marker. The new requirement worked on the first tree that violated it and that tree
was mine. Fixture updated; nothing was loosened to accommodate it.

RUNNING TALLY OF MY OWN DEFECTS IN THIS ONE GATE, all found by probing rather than rereading:
  1. substring match — a README saying "NOT MIT licensed" satisfied a decision of MIT (125d8b4);
  2. per-component blindness — option D splits would have passed unchecked (569b192);
  3. this one — the claim rule stopped being enforced at resolution.
All three shared a shape: the check was present and looked reasonable, and could not fail in the
direction that mattered. That is the same class the wave has been finding all day in each other's
work, and I do not think my rate is better than anyone's — I just probed my own gate three times.

comments.text:
FG-062 CONTINUATION at ff9cdf2 — covered the non-OSI resolution end to end, and the new test found a
FOURTH defect in this gate. STILL BLOCKED on the repository owner's D14 ruling.

THE GAP I CLOSED. Options A-D are OSI-approved and relax the open-source-claim rule. Option E
(Business Source / Functional Source) is a RESOLVED decision that is explicitly NOT open source, so
the repository must keep saying source-available for the whole restriction period. That is the
outcome where a stray "FrankenGit is open source" does the most damage, and it was the least covered:
my existing assertions proved only that the scan WOULD run under a non-OSI decision, never that the
pipeline actually catches a violation there.

Three new assertions. Two fixtures differing ONLY in the osi marker — the same planted claim is caught
under `no` and permitted under `yes`. A third asserts the gate accepts a consistently-stated BSL-1.1
outcome, because option E is a legitimate resolution and not an error state.

THE SCAN IS NOW A FUNCTION USED BY BOTH the live check and the fixtures. A fixture driving a
reimplementation would prove only that the reimplementation works, which is the fixture-only hazard
AGENTS.md names outright.

THE NEW TEST IMMEDIATELY FOUND A REAL BUG, which is the whole argument for having written it. The
scan's exclusion was an absolute `grep -v '/target/'`, and the harness allocates scratch directories
under target/e2e-artifacts/ — so the scan silently matched nothing and reported clean. Against the
live repository it happened to behave, so the defect was invisible; the first fixture that lived in a
harness tempdir exposed it immediately.

Same shape as the other three: the check could not fail in the direction that mattered. A checker
whose exclusion is wide enough to swallow its own input reports "no claims found" for exactly the
reason it should be reporting a finding. Fixed by making the exclusion root-relative — scan `.` from
inside the root and drop `./target/`, so the repository's build output is excluded while a fixture
tree (which has no target/) stays fully visible.

RUNNING TALLY OF MY OWN DEFECTS IN THIS ONE GATE, all found by probing rather than rereading:
  1. substring match — a README saying "NOT MIT licensed" satisfied a decision of MIT (125d8b4)
  2. per-component blindness — option D splits would have passed unchecked (569b192)
  3. the claim rule stopped being enforced once any decision landed (88a29a6)
  4. the scan's own exclusion swallowed its input, reporting clean (ff9cdf2)
Four defects, four different mechanisms, one shared property: each check was present, looked
reasonable, and could not fail where it mattered.

comments.author: JadeFalcon
comments.text:
BLOCKER, stated per acceptance line rather than for the bead as a whole —
because I have been describing this bead imprecisely and two of its four lines
are NOT blocked.

I have been reporting fg062 as "owner-gated on Jeff's D14 ruling", full stop.
That is true of the DECISION and it is true of lines 1 and 2. It is NOT true of
lines 3 and 4, which are about handling the decision's ABSENCE and need no
ruling at all. Correcting my own framing, and verifying rather than asserting.

Measured at 99ed758.

LINE 1 — "decision recorded in docs/LICENSING_DECISION.md with rationale and the
exact texts"
  BLOCKED, and correctly so. The document says outright at line 26: "Nothing in
  this document decides D14. The choice is the repository owner's." Not mine to
  make, and GoldLotus has already ruled it is not theirs either.
  Marker state today: `unresolved`; OSI marker: `unknown`.

LINE 2 — "LICENSE, README, CONTRIBUTING, Cargo license metadata and any
generated status all consistent on day one of the change"
  BLOCKED, downstream of line 1. There is no way to make artefacts consistent
  with a decision that does not exist. The MACHINERY that will enforce the
  consistency exists and is tested (20 assertions in the license lane); what is
  missing is the content it will enforce.

LINE 3 — "if the decision is deferred at any release point, the release refuses
(wire it into the fg035 release checklist)"
  DONE, and verified LIVE rather than structurally. scripts/verify.sh
  run_release() checks the D14 gate FIRST and on its own (verify.sh:69-77).
  Running it right now:

    $ ./scripts/license_gate.sh
    license-gate: REFUSED: D14 (license model) is UNRESOLVED.
    license-gate:   A release may not ship under a provisional source-available rider.
    exit 3

  The reason it is a separate gate that runs first is recorded in
  LICENSING_DECISION.md under "Why deferral is enforced rather than remembered":
  `verify.sh release` already refuses today, but only because no releasable
  binary exists, and that refusal disappears the moment FG-035/FG-091 make
  releases real. A launch-blocking requirement riding on an unrelated temporary
  refusal is not enforced — it has merely never been tested. Ordering the D14
  gate first means lifting the dormancy refusal cannot silently lift this one
  with it.

LINE 4 — "no doc anywhere claims open source until the license actually is"
  DONE. The lane's no-premature-open-source-claim step scans the WHOLE
  repository — `grep -rnEI --include='*.md' .` from the root, excluding only
  ./target/ and the lane's own fixtures. (The `fge_context scope` line naming
  four files is descriptive metadata, not the scan scope; I re-read the scan
  itself rather than trusting that string, because it would have been an easy
  and wrong way to conclude the check was narrow.)
  It matches ASSERTION shapes — "FrankenGit is open source", an OSI badge — and
  never the bare token, so the decision document can discuss open source freely.
  It keys on the OSI marker rather than on UNRESOLVED, so it does not go quiet
  the moment any decision lands — including a resolution to a non-OSI model,
  which is the outcome where a stray "open source" line does the most damage.

EVIDENCE AT 99ed758
  scripts/license_gate.sh                                  exit 3, refuses as designed
  scripts/e2e/suites/license/license_consistency.sh        20 assertions, 20 pass, exit 0

  Worktree qualification, since I have argued elsewhere that results must not be
  bound to a SHA over a dirty tree: `git status --porcelain` is NON-empty
  (fgit-authority, fgit-authority-fsqlite, fgit-statistics, Cargo.lock, .beads,
  and two untracked dirs — all other agents' in-flight work). I checked every
  dirty path against this lane's inputs (docs/*.md, LICENSE, README.md,
  CONTRIBUTING.md, crates/*/Cargo.toml, scripts/license_gate.sh) and NONE
  intersect. So the binding holds, and I am stating the intersection check
  rather than waving the dirt away.

  Correcting one earlier number of mine: I previously reported this lane as
  having 22 assertions. That came from grepping fge_assert/fge_pass/fge_fail
  occurrences, which counts both branches of an if/else. The executed count is
  20. The measured number is the right one.

WHAT WOULD UNBLOCK THIS BEAD
  Exactly one thing: the repository owner selects the licence model. Then lines
  1 and 2 are a single commit — set the two markers in LICENSING_DECISION.md,
  write the rationale and exact texts, and update LICENSE / README /
  CONTRIBUTING / Cargo metadata in the same commit, which is what line 2's "on
  day one" requires. The gate and the claim scan then stop refusing on their
  own; neither needs editing to accommodate the answer, whatever it is. Option D
  (a per-component split) is the one case that needs the gate extended, and
  LICENSING_DECISION.md already says that extension lands in the same commit as
  the split rather than as a follow-up.

  I am not going to sit on this bead waiting. Per GoldLotus's instruction I am
  not burning cycles on the decision itself, and the two lines I CAN do are
  done. If the orchestrator would rather this bead not hold an in_progress slot
  while it waits on an owner decision, moving it to blocked is reasonable — that
  is their call, not mine, and I am not self-transitioning it.

OpenAI/Anthropic rider. Recorded as LicenseRef-MIT-OpenAI-Anthropic-Rider with the OSI marker
set to `no`.

1. "decision recorded in docs/LICENSING_DECISION.md with rationale and the exact texts"
   -> markers flipped UNRESOLVED/unknown -> LicenseRef-MIT-OpenAI-Anthropic-Rider / no, with
      the rationale, the OSI reasoning, and provenance (owner's words, relay, timestamp).

2. "LICENSE, README licensing sections, CONTRIBUTING, Cargo license metadata, and any generated
    status all consistent on day one"
   -> scripts/license_gate.sh exit 0: "D14 resolved as 'LicenseRef-MIT-OpenAI-Anthropic-Rider'

      (license-file = "LICENSE", satisfied) and every crate declaring its own licence.

3. "if the decision is deferred at any release point, the release refuses (wire into fg035)"
   -> ALREADY SATISFIED before today, and I verified rather than assumed it: verify.sh
      run_release() calls license_gate.sh FIRST and on its own, explicitly so the launch-blocking
      requirement does not ride on the temporary dormancy refusal that FG-035/FG-091 will remove.

4. "no doc anywhere claims open source until the license actually is"
   -> the suite's live claim scan runs whenever the OSI marker is not `yes`. Mine is `no`, so it
      RAN against the real repository and found nothing. 22/22 assertions pass.

THE INTERPRETATION QUESTION, AND WHY I DID NOT TAKE THE CONVENIENT READING. The ruling says
AGENTS.md S10 "wrongly states 'source-available, not OSI open source' -- it is MIT+rider". That
could be read as "stop saying it is not open source". I did not read it that way, and the
artifacts decide it rather than my judgement:

  - the LICENSE text withholds all rights from named parties, which the Open Source Definition
    forbids, so the terms cannot be OSI-approved however permissive the MIT core is;
  - LICENSING_DECISION.md's own rule says that under `no` the repository MUST keep saying
    source-available for as long as the restriction lasts;
  - this bead's acceptance line 4 says no doc may claim open source until the licence actually is.

So the correction is that S10 was VAGUE, not that it was wrong about OSI: it described the terms
without naming them. Every surface now names LicenseRef-MIT-OpenAI-Anthropic-Rider AND states it
is not OSI-approved, because both are true and the second is required. If the owner meant the
stronger reading, this is one line to change and I would rather be told than write a false public
licensing claim on my own initiative.

EVIDENCE THAT THE GREEN MEANS SOMETHING. A passing gate proves nothing until it is shown to fail,
and this gate's own comments record that its first implementation used grep -qF, so under a
decision of MIT a README reading "This project is NOT MIT licensed" satisfied it. Negative
controls, run against CONTRIBUTING.md and restored byte-identical:

  terms absent                     -> exit 3 REFUSED
  terms present but DENIED         -> exit 3 REFUSED
  restored                         -> exit 0 OK

The denial case is the one that matters, and it confirms the negation filter works for THIS
identifier and not merely for the historical MIT example.

THE ONE THING I CHANGED THAT WAS NOT ASKED FOR, and why it would have been wrong not to.
scripts/e2e/suites/license/license_consistency.sh asserted, against the LIVE repository, that the
gate refuses with exit 3 "while the decision is deferred". Resolving D14 falsifies that. Flipping
it to 0 would have been the whole fix -- and would have silently deleted coverage, because that
live check was the ONLY place the gate's UNRESOLVED -> 3 behaviour was exercised; everything else
in the suite is fixture-based. A suite that stops testing a refusal at the moment the refusal
stops firing is RH-1 whether or not anyone intended it. So:

  fg062-gate-accepts-resolved-live      0   replaces it; the live repo must now pass
  fg062-gate-refuses-deferred           3   survives, on a scratch tree marked UNRESOLVED
  fg062-deferral-refusal-is-attributable 0  NEW

The third exists because my first fixture was over-determined: its placeholder surfaces stated no
identifier, so they would fail a RESOLVED gate too, and the refusal could not distinguish "the
marker says UNRESOLVED" from "the surfaces were junk". The fixture now states a real identifier
consistently and the twin flips ONLY the marker, requiring exit 0. One difference between refusal
and pass is what makes the refusal attributable to the marker.

GATES at HEAD dffc077 / my commit 48b43ab:
  scripts/license_gate.sh                             exit 0

inspection that registry-check's one licence assertion (main.rs:1254, README must contain

SHARED-TREE INCIDENT, reported because it affects where the evidence lives. My LICENSE, README,
CONTRIBUTING, AGENTS.md and VERIFY_SPEC edits were committed by someone else while I was still
working, at 5a25ed1 and 70a18f3. Content landed INTACT -- those paths are clean against my final

title: FG-063: Federation and local-first collaboration phase
description:
GOAL
The plan section 23 capability (subsequent scope, tracked now so it is never lost): offline-first operation against exact capsules, signed immutable bundle exchange, federation classes (objects/capsules, mirror observations, proposed ref transactions, social events, PR/review/evidence bundles, release attestations, org/policy assertions), and equivocation-evidence handling.

WHY / BACKGROUND
The iron law (23.3): ref authority is NEVER CRDT ambiguity — a remote protected-branch head merges by proposal (immutable observation, mirror-namespace ref, proposed RefTxn with expected basis, equivocation witness, or review item), and local authority decides; last-writer-wins on canonical state is unrepresentable. CALM-friendly social state (23.4): append-only comments/attestations/reactions may replicate coordination-free when their algebra and retractions are explicit; moderation/deletion/permissions/protection/billing/holds require local ordered decisions. Offline bundles (23.5) carry basis capsule/RCR + intents/effects/evidence + capability constraints, and import ALWAYS revalidates current policy/witnesses — an offline success proves nothing about applicability now. Depends on the D13 ADR (fg061) for the trust/moderation model.

ACCEPTANCE
- offline work bundle round-trip: create offline against a capsule, import online, revalidation catches a staged conflict fixture;
- mirror-namespace and proposed-RefTxn flows implemented; direct remote-head merge into canonical refs is unrepresentable;
- equivocation fixture (one peer signs conflicting claims) produces durable evidence and review-surface routing;
- federated event classes each declare monotone/CRDT/coordinated per the CALM registry (new rows added as needed).

TEST PLAN: bundle round-trip unit tests; two-instance e2e scripts/e2e/federation_bundles.sh registered in run_all.sh.

CONSTITUTIONAL CONSTRAINTS (AGENTS.md; non-negotiable)
- Pure Rust, edition 2024, dated-nightly pin from rust-toolchain.toml; every first-party crate carries #![forbid(unsafe_code)]; no C/C++ FFI, no C Git/libgit2/JGit/Dulwich/gix, no hidden subprocess fallback. Upstream Git binaries are pinned, sandboxed differential ORACLES only (never production).
- Asupersync is the sole async runtime (no Tokio/async-std/smol). Long-lived work owns children via regions; cancellation is request -> drain -> finalize; effects use typed obligations (Reserved -> Committed -> Acknowledged, or Reserved -> Aborted).
- Closed dependency universe: every crate (incl. transitive, enforced via Cargo.lock scan) must match an active allow row in registries/dependency_policy.tsv. No build scripts/proc macros without a constitutional exception. No network during builds.
- Final-abstraction slices only: no empty crates, no HashMap-pretending-to-be-storage, no fixture-only parser wired as production API. A subset is fine when its unsupported surface is a typed refusal.
- Claim lattice (invariant > proof > bounded model > statistical > SLO > benchmark): never describe this work as stronger than its evidence. Record disproven hypotheses in docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE_LEDGER.md + registries/negative_evidence.tsv.
- Run ./scripts/verify.sh fast before and after; stage only intended files; keep generated artifacts out of source.

title: FG-067: Benchmark evidence harness and required system-metric suites (VERIFY section 23, E5)
description:
GOAL
The performance/economic evidence machinery the plan section 38.4 proof contract and VERIFY_SPEC section 23 require and every benchmark-bearing bead (fg014b, fg017b, fg020b, fg028c, fg036c) presupposes: a pinned benchmark-artifact schema with A/A controls, tail capture, environment fingerprints, correctness oracles, rollback artifacts, and the required system-metric families.

WHY / BACKGROUND
"A microbenchmark win cannot justify an end-to-end claim" and "a lower-lane lock-contention microbenchmark cannot establish repository throughput" (VERIFY_SPEC:226) are constitutional (NEG-014/NEG-016). Every benchmark artifact must contain source/tree/lock/toolchain/OS/CPU/target/build profile, dataset/workload, warm/cold/cache state, commands/env allowlist, baseline/candidate/A-A, raw samples, tails, correctness oracle, and replay/rollback (VERIFY_SPEC:522). Without ONE shared harness, each benchmark bead invents its own schema and cross-bead comparison rots. The 7-item optimization-admission checklist (DEPENDENCY_AND_MEMORY_SAFETY_CONSTITUTION.md:105-113) gates every optimization on this harness. This is distinct from fg054 (statistical ADAPTATION controllers) and fg055 (claim routing) — it is the measurement substrate they and every perf bead build on.

DELIVERABLES: benchmark-artifact schema (fg002 codec); a runner capturing environment fingerprint + raw samples + tails + A/A control + correctness-oracle results; the required system-metric suites (latency/throughput tails, CPU, memory, object requests, egress, storage amplification per section 39.2, decisions-per-CAS); the optimization-admission checklist as a gate.

ACCEPTANCE
- artifact schema with reproduction command; A/A control demonstrates the noise floor before any A/B claim is admissible;
- correctness oracle runs concurrently (a benchmark that disables verification measures a different system — refused);
- fg014b/fg017b/fg020b/fg028c/fg036c migrate onto this harness (follow-up notes added when it lands);
- disproven-speedup path writes the negative-evidence ledger automatically.

TEST PLAN: harness self-test with a known-cost workload; e2e scripts/e2e/benchmark_harness.sh registered in run_all.sh.

CONSTITUTIONAL CONSTRAINTS (AGENTS.md; non-negotiable)
- Pure Rust, edition 2024, dated-nightly pin from rust-toolchain.toml; every first-party crate carries #![forbid(unsafe_code)]; no C/C++ FFI, no C Git/libgit2/JGit/Dulwich/gix, no hidden subprocess fallback. Upstream Git binaries are pinned, sandboxed differential ORACLES only (never production).
- Asupersync is the sole async runtime (no Tokio/async-std/smol). Long-lived work owns children via regions; cancellation is request -> drain -> finalize; effects use typed obligations (Reserved -> Committed -> Acknowledged, or Reserved -> Aborted).
- Closed dependency universe: every crate (incl. transitive, enforced via Cargo.lock scan) must match an active allow row in registries/dependency_policy.tsv. No build scripts/proc macros without a constitutional exception. No network during builds.
- Final-abstraction slices only: no empty crates, no HashMap-pretending-to-be-storage, no fixture-only parser wired as production API. A subset is fine when its unsupported surface is a typed refusal.
- Claim lattice (invariant > proof > bounded model > statistical > SLO > benchmark): never describe this work as stronger than its evidence. Record disproven hypotheses in docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE_LEDGER.md + registries/negative_evidence.tsv.
- Run ./scripts/verify.sh fast before and after; stage only intended files; keep generated artifacts out of source.

---
## EMBEDDED NORMATIVE CONTENT (verbatim from the design docs; self-contained — do not consult the source markdown)

### Benchmark artifact required fields (VERIFY_SPEC §23 / plan §38.4 proof contract)

Every benchmark artifact contains: source/tree/lock/toolchain/OS/CPU/target/build profile; dataset/workload; warm/cold/cache state; commands/environment allowlist; baseline/candidate/A-A control; raw samples; tails (p95/p99); CPU; memory; object requests; egress; storage amplification (SA = (canonical + repair + replica + retained derived) / logical reachable Git bytes, reported by class); decisions-per-CAS; correctness oracle (run CONCURRENTLY — a benchmark that disables verification measures a different system); replay/rollback artifact. Hard rules: a microbenchmark win cannot justify an end-to-end claim; a lower-lane lock-contention microbenchmark cannot establish repository throughput (NEG-014); disproven-speedup hypotheses land in the negative-evidence ledger (NEG-016). The 7-item optimization-admission checklist (ordering/tie-break/FP/RNG/codec equivalence; environment fingerprint; A-A control; raw samples+tails; resource+economic impact; rollback; negative result) gates every optimization.

title: FG-068: Toolchain-refresh lane for dated-nightly advancement (D15)
description:
GOAL
The recurring local lane that DEPENDENCY_AND_MEMORY_SAFETY_CONSTITUTION.md:81-84 requires: propose the next nightly, run the complete gate matrix against it, record compiler/LLVM fingerprints and performance deltas, and emit the evidence pack that authorizes (or refuses) the rust-toolchain.toml pin-bump commit.

WHY / BACKGROUND
A toolchain advancement is a MATERIAL change (AGENTS.md 3.4): the pinned nightly is refreshed frequently but only by an explicit commit whose evidence pack proves behavior and performance did not regress. fg061's D15 ADR records the CADENCE POLICY; this bead builds the LANE that executes it — distinct from the checker (fg001x, which validates the pin is dated) and release (fg035). Without it, every nightly bump is an unevidenced leap of faith, and toolchain regressions (miscompiles, perf cliffs, lint churn) land silently.

ACCEPTANCE
- lane runs end to end against a candidate nightly and emits the evidence pack;
- a seeded regression (e.g. a new clippy denial or a perf threshold breach) refuses the bump with typed evidence;
- the evidence pack is what a pin-bump commit references; a bump without it is flagged (checker hook);
- compiler/LLVM fingerprints recorded for reproducibility.

comments.author: JadeFalcon
comments.text:
FG-068 COMPLETE at 2adf194 — the lane that executes ADR-0010's D15 cadence. Suite 15/15 exit 0.

ADR-0010 recorded the cadence policy; nothing executed it, so every nightly bump was an unevidenced
leap of faith on a change AGENTS.md 3.4 calls material.

THREE DESIGN POINTS THAT ARE THE ACTUAL WORK:
  1. It never moves the pin. ADR-0010 clause 3 requires an advancement to be one commit that moves
     rust-toolchain.toml and nothing else; a lane that edited the pin would let evidence and change
     land together unexamined. It only ever produces — or refuses to produce — the pack such a
     commit cites.
  2. A refused candidate leaves NO pack. A pack recording its own failure could still be cited by a
     bump, and a reader would reasonably take citing evidence as being authorised by it. Refusal has
     to be an absence, not a document.
  3. Toolchain identity is VERIFIED, not assumed. The fingerprint describes the ACTIVE compiler,
     which is not automatically the candidate. If they differ, every gate result is attributed to a
     compiler that never produced it — a pack that is evidence about something it did not measure,
     and indistinguishable from a real one. Refuses before any gate runs; where rustup is absent it
     records `unverified` IN THE PACK rather than silently guessing.

FOUND BY ACTUALLY RUNNING IT, which a stub could never have taught me. Pointed at the real
verify.sh on this host the lane sat queued behind the shared cargo build lock — 40+ cargo processes
live — and would have hung indefinitely. An evidence lane that hangs yields neither evidence nor
refusal: nobody learns anything and the run merely looks slow. Each gate now runs under a wall-clock
ceiling.

A timed-out gate is INCONCLUSIVE, deliberately a third state rather than folded into failure. "The
gate said no" and "the gate never answered" call for different responses — investigate the candidate
versus re-run when the host is quiet — and collapsing them would send a reader chasing a toolchain
regression that was really lock contention. Both still block the pack; only an affirmative pass
authorises a bump.

--verify-bump is the checker hook the acceptance line asks for: it answers only "is the checked-in
pin backed by a pack naming it?", runs no gates, and is cheap enough for a pre-commit guard. A decoy
pack naming a different candidate is rejected, or the check degrades into "some pack exists".

EVIDENCE, revision-bound at 2adf194:
  scripts/e2e/suites/toolchain/toolchain_refresh.sh = 15 assertions, 15 passed, 0 failed, exit 0,
                                                      duplicate_ids empty
  refusal paths each exit 3 leaving no pack          = inconclusive, regression, identity mismatch,
                                                      decoy pack, missing evidence
  shellcheck -S warning on both files                = clean
  auto-discovered by run_all.sh                      = yes (39 suites)
No cargo test/clippy/build was run for this bead; it adds no Rust.

NOT CLAIMED, and this is the load-bearing limitation: the e2e INJECTS the gate runner. That proves
the lane's logic — fingerprinting, identity, comparison, refusal, pack emission — and proves nothing
about docs/constitution/fast, which have their own lanes. A green run of this lane means "the gates
I was told to run reported success", never "the toolchain is good".

ALSO NOT DONE, named rather than buried:
  - I did NOT install a candidate nightly. That is a networked, shared-machine action outside what I
    should take unilaterally, so no toolchain other than the active one was really evaluated; the
    identity guard is exercised by naming a candidate that is deliberately not active.
  - The full real-verify.sh run did not complete inside my window because of the lock contention
    above. I am not claiming it as evidence.
  - The bead's deliverables mention running the fg067 benchmark suite for perf deltas. The lane does
    NOT do this, and the pack says so in a not_covered row rather than staying silent. Wiring the
    benchmark comparison is real remaining work and I did not smuggle it into "done".

comments.author: SnowyFortress
comments.text:
CLAIMED by SnowyFortress (cc_1). Read-only investigation first, at 3953626. Two findings materially change this bead, so I am reporting before building anything rather than after.

METHOD: cargo metadata --locked (the same query scripts/verify.sh already runs; no build), classifying every resolved package by target kind, then diffing against registries/dependency_policy.tsv.

FINDING 1 — THE REGISTRY CANNOT EXPRESS WHAT THE CONSTITUTION REQUIRES IT TO. This is deliverable 1's real blocker.
Resolved graph at 3953626: 249 packages, 14 with a proc-macro target, 37 with a build script (custom-build target).
DEPENDENCY_AND_MEMORY_SAFETY_CONSTITUTION.md:144 requires 'The local verifier enumerates every enabled build script and proc macro and compares it with the dependency registry.'
But registries/dependency_policy.tsv is franken-registry-v1 with exactly ten columns: id, crate_pattern, scope, decision, owner, rationale, feature_policy, unsafe_policy, ffi_policy, status. NONE of them can declare 'this crate has a build script' or 'this crate is a proc macro'. There is nothing to compare against.
Today 14 proc-macro crates carry the string 'proc_macro_transitive' in the unsafe_policy column — a convention overloading a field meant for unsafe policy, not a schema field. All 14 proc-macro packages happen to be covered by it. ZERO of the 37 build-script packages are declarable at all: anyhow, asupersync, bincode-next, blake3, crc32c, crc32fast, crossbeam-deque, crossbeam-epoch, crossbeam-utils, curve25519-dalek, generic-array, getrandom, iana-time-zone-haiku, io-uring, libc, memoffset, nix, ntapi, num-traits, objc2, parking_lot_core, proc-macro2, quote, rustix, rustversion, serde, serde_core, serde_json, signal-hook, thiserror, wasm-bindgen, wasm-bindgen-shared, winapi, winapi-i686-pc-windows-gnu, winapi-x86_64-pc-windows-gnu, zerocopy, zmij.
This is an AGENTS.md 15 stop condition (documents/registries contradict one another). Closing it needs a registry SCHEMA decision — two new columns, or a documented convention promoted to a real field — which is a shared-file change to registries/*.tsv AND tools/registry-check/** (CopperCondor's reserved area). GoldLotus: I need a ruling on the schema before I can write the enumeration check, and CopperCondor needs to be in that decision.

FINDING 2 — DELIVERABLE 2'S TARGET SET IS CURRENTLY EMPTY. The bead's stated motivation is 'Serde derives on canonical identity types (fg002) ARE authority-sensitive generated code: a proc-macro version bump could silently change derived encoding/decoding and thus IDENTITY.' That is no longer true of this codebase. NO first-party crate depends on serde, thiserror, prost, zerocopy, pin-project or bincode. There is not one #[derive(Serialize)] or #[derive(Deserialize)] anywhere under crates/*/src/. The only derives in first-party code are compiler built-ins (Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord), which are not proc macros from the dependency graph.
The reason is that ADR-0002 made the canonical codec HAND-OWNED: fgit-codec::Encoder is written by hand precisely so encoding is not derive-driven. I can confirm from the consumer side — fgit-treefs encodes snapshot bodies through that Encoder and derives nothing.
So building a cargo-expand-style golden-expansion harness right now would produce machinery guarding zero targets. Given the audit's finding that verification machinery is already more finished than the product, I am not going to build that on a premise the codebase has moved past.

With zero derives, the stronger and cheaper guard is a check that first-party crates acquire NO third-party derive macro on canonical types — turning today's accidental property into an asserted one, with a live consumer (the constitution lane) and a real defect class (a future serde derive silently entering fgit-types or fgit-codec). Steps 2-4 can be one commit; step 1 cannot be skipped or reordered. Nothing I hold is landable before it.

## Deliverable 2 is drafted too (ruling 5) — and it needed no denylist
Mechanical rule: a first-party manifest may not declare a direct dependency on a package that either IS a proc macro, or AT ITS RESOLVED FEATURES directly depends on one. Those are precisely the packages that can hand a derive to first-party code.

Measured at e5c745a, direct proc-macro edges:

  serde [serde_derive]   thiserror [thiserror-impl]   prost [prost-derive]
  pin-project [pin-project-internal]           bincode-next [bincode_derive-next, pastey]
  zerocopy []            <- at OUR resolved features (simd); with `derive` it would pull zerocopy-derive

- a renamed dependency (`harmless = { package = "serde" }`, inline and table) that must not launder past;
- a direct dependency on the proc-macro crate itself;
- feature-awareness: same manifest line, derive edge off then on;
- the real DEP-003 serde* / DEP-219 serde_derive precedence collision;

- dev edges followed from members but not from dependencies; build edges counting as enabled; disabled-vs-absent; not_applicable; state word round-trip.
