title: fgit-atp-git: the payload-identity and probabilistic-summary refusals are the last public cluster left in AtpRefusal
description:
MEASURED per variant with a both-trees grep; crates/fgit-atp-git/src has no suite-like module, so a tests/ scan is sound (checked). After 0k6d, 78ra, sezr and 2gzj, this is the last cluster reachable through public API. Five variants:

  NativeObjectIdentityMismatch  PUB TransferObjectEntry::from_payload
  PayloadLengthMismatch         verify_payload, reached from PUB reconstruct
  InvalidProbabilisticSummary   checked_summary_byte_count, reached from PUB from_wire and PUB insert -- TWO axes
  PlanManifestMismatch          PUB reconstruct
  InventoryTooLarge             ensure_inventory_count, reached from PUB exact_objects AND PUB exact_segments -- TWO sites

THE PROPERTY WORTH PINNING. from_payload RE-DERIVES the native Git object id
from the bytes and refuses a mismatch, so an identity is not something a caller
gets to assert. 0k6d relied on that when it computed orderings rather than
assuming them, and CloudyTiger's fixture in fabric_fault_suite.rs records the
same lesson from the other side -- its first version invented an identity and
was correctly refused. Nothing names the variant, so the property everything
else leans on is itself untested.

TWO AXES, TWO SITES.
  InvalidProbabilisticSummary fires on bit_count == 0 OR bit_count not a
  multiple of 8. Two ways to be wrong in one condition; a probe using zero
  leaves the alignment axis unexercised and vice versa.
  InventoryTooLarge is reached from exact_objects and from exact_segments.
  A refusal through one says nothing about the other; both get a probe.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. Every variant its own probe NAMING it and asserting its payload where carried -- NativeObjectIdentityMismatch carries the claimed identity, PayloadLengthMismatch and InventoryTooLarge carry offered/maximum pairs.
2. InvalidProbabilisticSummary gets TWO probes, one per axis. InventoryTooLarge gets TWO, one per call site.
3. PERMITTED TWINS, BUILT FIRST AND MADE TO PASS BEFORE ANY REFUSAL PROBE. A payload whose DERIVED identity is used constructs; a summary with a non-zero multiple-of-8 bit count constructs; an inventory at EXACTLY max_objects is admitted, since that guard reads greater-than rather than greater-or-equal. This ordering has caught a real fixture error on three of my last eight beads.
4. THE IDENTITY PROBE MUST DERIVE, NEVER INVENT. Compute the real object id for the payload and use it for the accepted case; for the refusal, hand a DIFFERENT real identity rather than random bytes, so the refusal is about mismatch rather than about malformed input.
5. ORDERING: at least one probe wrong TWICE, reporting the earlier fault. Remember both boundaries already measured -- a reorder and a deletion need different probes (ydpc), and a TIGHTENED guard is invisible to every refusal probe with only accepted-path tests catching it (2gzj).
6. MUTATION-VERIFIED: drop the multiple-of-8 term from checked_summary_byte_count, so a misaligned bit count is admitted while zero still refuses. That is invisible to a probe using only the zero axis, which is the point of acceptance 2. Report which tests fall AND which do not, INCLUDING whether the crate's inline module notices -- on xd45 it did, unlike the eight crates before it, so do not assume. fgit-atp-git is a default-members crate, so cargo check the mutated tree BEFORE running anything else.
7. WHERE: a NEW test file. atp_delta_campaign.sh drives fallback_reasons, payload_integrity, summary_poisoning, abandonment_visibility, trust_scope_isolation and --lib BY NAME; a new target is not among them. Verify rather than assume.
8. NON-CLAIM: state how many AtpRefusal variants remain unnamed after this, and separate newly-covered from any site found unreachable. If reconstruct's fixture proves disproportionate, say so and leave those two open rather than stretching the file -- 9xyg left the certificate pair open for exactly that reason.

Tests only; no src change.

title: fgit-authority: the refusal arm of the linearizability trace codec is encoded by no test, so every recorded refusal is unverified
description:
MEASURED. AuthorityRefusal has twelve variants. Nine are named by behavioural tests in this crate (UnknownVersionToken, TokenKeyMismatch, TokenGenerationMismatch, TokenBodyMismatch, NonMonotoneGeneration, BodyTooLarge, HeadAbsent, Throttled, Unavailable). Three are named by nothing: InvalidKey, CapacityExhausted, OperationUnsupported.

BUT THE PER-VARIANT COUNT UNDERSTATES IT, and that is the point of this bead. Those nine are named where a STORE refuses. None of the twelve is ever encoded. write_refusal (history.rs:784) and read_refusal (history.rs:847) -- tag 6 of the response codec and all twelve refusal tags beneath it -- are exercised by NO test:

  tests/lincheck_codec.rs is the only file that encodes a History, and its
  fixture_history() contains exactly one response, AuthorityResponse::ReadHead(HeadRead::Absent).
  It contains no refusal at all.

  tests/fault_campaign.rs BUILDS AuthorityResponse::Refused values, which is why
  a grep looks reassuring, but it only compares them behaviourally -- it calls
  AuthorityHistory::new and never encodes the result.

So a grep for the variant names finds behavioural assertions and reports a false green over the codec.

WHY THE CODEC IS THE SURFACE THAT MATTERS HERE. This crate's history codec is how a linearizability trace becomes an artifact. Section 10 requires public quantitative claims to be machine-derived or artifact-linked, and section 9 classifies verifier independence; a trace codec that mangles a refusal silently corrupts the evidence rather than failing. A behavioural test proves the store refused. Only a round-trip proves the RECORD of that refusal survives being written and read back.

Three specific claims currently rest on nothing:

1. Every variant round-trips. Four carry payloads -- InvalidKey(KeyError), BodyTooLarge{len,limit}, CapacityExhausted{occupancy,limit}, NonMonotoneGeneration{..} -- and a variant that round-tripped its tag but dropped its payload would satisfy any bare variant match.

2. history.rs:868 comments that tag 11 (OperationUnsupported) is "additive: no previously recorded trace can contain it, so existing goldens decode unchanged". That is a WIRE-COMPATIBILITY claim and nothing tests it. tests/goldens/lincheck/authority_history_v1.hex exists and is the artifact the claim is about.

3. KeyError itself has two shapes (Empty, TooLong{len,limit}) inside InvalidKey, so the nested payload has its own axes.

SECOND, SEPARABLE GAP IN THE SAME VARIANT. OperationUnsupported is produced by the DEFAULT bodies of AuthorityStore::publish_head_with_outcomes (contract.rs:198) and its async twin (async_contract.rs:320). Nothing asserts either default actually refuses -- yet THREE crates' test doubles reason about that behaviour in comments (fgit-compaction/tests/compaction_protocol.rs:465, fgit-admission/tests/async_admission_equivalence.rs:180, fgit-chronicle/tests/capsule_pointer.rs:668), and this crate's own AsyncView in tests/async_seal_admission.rs silently inherits it by not overriding the method.

That is the failure mode where a two-surface equivalence test reports "unsupported/refused" and the cause is the MOCK inheriting a refuse-by-design default rather than a broken surface. The doubles are right to rely on it; nothing has checked that they may.

ACCEPTANCE.

1. Every one of the twelve AuthorityRefusal variants round-trips through the history codec, exhaustively rather than sampled, with its payload asserted where it carries one. Driven by encoding a History that contains the refusal as a response and decoding it back, so tag 6 is exercised too -- not by calling write_refusal directly, which is private.

2. The twelve encodings are pairwise DISTINCT. Twelve variants that all round-tripped to the same bytes would satisfy a per-variant round-trip and none of the intent.

3. The additive claim for tag 11 is checked against the actual artifact: tests/goldens/lincheck/authority_history_v1.hex still decodes to the same history. If the golden cannot carry a refusal, say so and state what the check does and does not cover.

4. The nested KeyError payload probed on both shapes, and the numeric payloads (len/limit, occupancy/limit) asserted by VALUE, not merely by variant.

5. BOTH trait defaults asserted to refuse with OperationUnsupported -- the sync one directly, the async one through the poll_ready helper already in tests/async_seal_admission.rs -- and asserted to AGREE. This is the assumption three crates' doubles are built on.

6. Mutation matrix per the standing ruling, two-sided. Swapping two refusal tags is the mutation this bead exists to catch: every behavioural test stays green because the store still refuses correctly; only a round-trip notices the record is wrong.

NON-CLAIM: this covers the RECORD of a refusal, not the decision to raise one. It says nothing about whether any store refuses in the right circumstances, and CapacityExhausted's live construction sites are in fgit-authority-fsqlite (engine.rs:556, :678, :687), so this bead does not test that backend's capacity guards -- only that the variant survives being recorded.

comments.text:
CORRECTION to this bead's own description, before writing a line of test.

I wrote that "this crate's own AsyncView in tests/async_seal_admission.rs silently inherits it by not overriding the method". THAT IS WRONG. AsyncView DOES override publish_head_with_outcomes, delegating to the wrapped MemoryAuthorityStore (tests/async_seal_admission.rs:123). I read the first half of that impl and inferred the rest.

The corrected picture is STRONGER than what I filed, not weaker. The default's behaviour is load-bearing in BOTH directions, and each direction is documented in a different crate:

- fgit-chronicle/tests/capsule_pointer.rs:666 DELIBERATELY does not override it. Its comment: the default refusal "is exactly what an explicit override in this view would say", and it matters because that view wraps MemoryAuthorityStore, which composes a head CAS and separate puts, so any delegating implementation "would be NON-atomic while satisfying the signature -- a fixture that looks like it publishes atomically and does not, which a later test could pass against and be read as evidence the FG-007b window is closed." Inheriting the refusal "keeps the safe answer as the one you get by doing nothing."

- fgit-admission/tests/async_admission_equivalence.rs:176 forwards it explicitly and records a REAL PAST INCIDENT from not doing so: "Leaving it on the default made this fixture refuse every commit while the blocking surface committed -- which read as the two surfaces disagreeing about the shared core when in fact the fixture never reached it."

So one crate's correctness depends on the default REFUSING, another crate was burned when it refused unexpectedly, and a third and fourth (fgit-authority's own AsyncView, fgit-compaction's AmbiguousPublishStore) override it. Four test doubles make a deliberate decision about this default and NOTHING ASSERTS WHAT IT DOES.

Acceptance line 5 stands unchanged and is now better motivated: assert both defaults refuse with OperationUnsupported and agree. Added to it: a PERMITTED TWIN showing a store that DOES implement the operation is not refused, so the test distinguishes "the default refuses" from "this operation always refuses".

No other acceptance line is affected. The codec gap -- lines 1 to 4, which is the bulk of this bead -- was measured directly and is unchanged.

Both directions are load-bearing: fgit-chronicle's capsule view DELIBERATELY inherits it (delegating there would be non-atomic while satisfying the signature), and fgit-admission's async view forwards it explicitly, recording the incident from not doing so -- leaving it on the default made that fixture refuse every commit while the blocking surface committed, which read as a two-surface disagreement when the fixture never reached the shared core.

          21 other test binaries   0 failed   BLIND
          this file                2 failed   caught it
     M2 Throttled writes Unavailable's tag, so a shed request is recorded as an endpoint rejection
          21 other test binaries   0 failed   BLIND
          this file                2 failed   caught it

COMPLETENESS ENFORCED AT COMPILE TIME. A hand-written list of an enum's variants is exactly the closed vocabulary that acquires a silent gap, so the file carries an exhaustive match with no wildcard: adding a variant to AuthorityRefusal makes this file fail to COMPILE rather than quietly test eleven.

TWO THINGS THAT COST AN ITERATION, recorded so nobody spends them again. The DuplicateAbsenceWitness has no public constructor on purpose -- its doc says minting belongs to the duplicate-detection walk, not to callers, because a public constructor would make it a token anyone can forge -- so the tests mint a real one through scan_for_existing_decisions. And the head must be a canonical RepositoryAuthorityHeadBody, not placeholder bytes: that walk DECODES what it reads, so a placeholder makes the scan fail with a codec fault instead of minting anything.

title: FG-030d: AGENT_PROTOCOL 4.3 refresh relations and the refreshed-authority receipt (unowned surface blocking fg030c)
description:
SCOPE: AGENT_PROTOCOL.md 4.3 (Refresh) plus the refreshed_authority_receipt field of the
10 ECC bundle. Implemented in crates/fgit-agent.

WHY THIS BEAD EXISTS. I measured the fg030 family and 4.3 is owned by NOBODY: fg030a
(IntentRun/capabilities/broker) closed, fg030b (ECC) closed, fg030c (adversarial corpus)
blocked, and no fourth sibling. TurquoiseWillow's fg030c block names a "refreshed-authority
publication witness" as one of four missing surfaces. I checked the other three and they
exist elsewhere -- fgit-treefs has the export boundary, fgit-resource has
ContextPacketComplete, fgit-evidence has EvidenceArtifact -- but this one has no
implementation anywhere. I searched every crate for "refresh" filtered to
authority/witness/receipt/basis/capability contexts and every hit is the ordinary English
word. So a P0 is blocked on a surface that no bead owns, which means it stays blocked.

CAVEAT ON THAT ABSENCE: a name search finds only uses that spell the name. Treat it as a
strong hypothesis, not proof, and re-check before writing code.

WHAT 4.3 ACTUALLY SPECIFIES (quoted, it is short):
  "A workspace never silently floats. Refresh creates a new receipt and one explicit
   relation:  FastForwarded; RebasedByIntentReplay; RebasedByStructuredPatch;
   MergedByDeclaredProof; ConflictRefused.
   The evidence record distinguishes checks performed before and after refresh."

And 10's bundle carries `refreshed_authority_receipt?` and `reconciliation_record?`.

DELIVERABLES
- the closed five-variant refresh relation, with ALL and stable wire code points assigned
  explicitly (not from declaration order), same discipline as EvidenceClass in ecc.rs;
- a refresh receipt binding the relation to the base it moved from and the base it moved to;
- EXACTLY ONE relation per refresh, unrepresentable rather than merely validated where the
  type system allows it;
- the before/after evidence distinction 4.3 requires: an evidence record states which side
  of the refresh its checks were performed on, and a bundle cannot silently present
  pre-refresh checks as covering the post-refresh state;
- wire it into EvidenceCarryingChange as the optional refreshed_authority_receipt, with the
  policy able to require it;
- codec round-trip and golden vectors via the existing independent generate.py.

ACCEPTANCE
- the five relations are structurally distinct, ALL is length-pinned against 4.3 in the
  same file as any test that iterates it (see the a-test-driven-from-all lesson: an
  ALL-driven loop silently shrinks when ALL does);
- a refresh carrying no relation, or more than one, is refused typed -- with the permitted
  twin (exactly one) accepted at the same shape;
- ConflictRefused is a REFUSAL outcome and must not satisfy a policy that requires a
  successful refresh; permitted twin: each of the other four does;
- evidence checked BEFORE a refresh does not count as covering the state after it; permitted
  twin: post-refresh checks do;
- a policy requiring a refreshed_authority_receipt refuses a bundle without one, typed;
  permitted twin: a bundle carrying one is accepted;
- UNREPORTED/absent is fail-closed throughout, per 9pdo -- do not reintroduce the defect
  where an unstated field reads as the permissive outcome;
- codec goldens regenerated from generate.py (a SECOND implementation, never blessed from
  encoder output) with the format change disclosed in the commit message;
- mutation matrix scored PER TEST, not in aggregate, including at least one over-strict
  mutation and one symmetric encoder+decoder mutation.

EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE, stated so the absence reads as scope rather than coverage
- PERFORMING the refresh. Rebasing, replaying intents, applying a structured patch or
  merging by declared proof are workspace operations and belong to fgit-treefs. This bead
  delivers the typed RECORD of what happened and its machine-checked constraints, which is
  what 10's bundle field needs and what an adversarial corpus can test against.
- The reconciliation_record, which is fg073's territory (Effect broker ledger and
  external-effect reconciliation).
- Anything requiring a real moving base; a receipt binds identities, it does not compute
  them.

NOTES
- fgit-agent is L2 and already depends on fgit-types, fgit-crypto, fgit-resource, fgit-codec.
  fgit-treefs is also L2, so a dependency on it would be layer-legal IF a later bead needs
  the performing half. This bead should not need it.
- crates/fgit-agent/src/lib.rs currently lists 4.3 under "What is deliberately not here".
  That paragraph must be updated in the same commit or it becomes a false statement.
- Filed by JadeFalcon while idle with a dry ready pool, after confirming no fg030 sibling
  and no other bead owns 4.3. If GoldLotus would rather this waited or belonged elsewhere,
  say so and I will stand down; filing it so the gap is tracked either way.

title: CALM-015 CacheGrant for authenticated materialization warming
description:
GOAL: implement the specified monotone_scoped CacheGrant for CALM-015 warm_authenticated_admission_materialization in fgit-resource.

title: e2e lib: fge_assert_match and fge_assert_no_file pass vacuously on an empty operand -- the same class already fixed for fge_assert_contains
description:
lib.sh already carries a long comment establishing the rule for this class, written after ChartreuseHorizon triaged 25 call sites: AN EMPTY NEEDLE IS ALWAYS A BUG, SO IT FAILS. fge_assert_contains enforces it with [ -n $needle ] and fge_assert_not_contains was hardened to match. Two siblings were never given the same treatment.

DEMONSTRATED, not argued, at this tree:
  fge_assert_match  lib.sh:2242   [[ $s =~ $re ]]
      an EMPTY regex matches EVERYTHING. Verified in bash: an empty pattern matches a non-empty
      string AND an empty string. So fge_assert_match ID $out $pattern with $pattern accidentally
      unset passes unconditionally -- the assertion cannot fail in the direction it exists to cover.
  fge_assert_no_file  lib.sh:2262   [ -e $p ]
      [ -e "" ] is FALSE, so an empty path records PASS. It reports the file is absent when no file
      was ever named.

Both are the empty-OPERAND case, not the empty-haystack case. The documented asymmetry does not apply: an unset pattern or an unset path is always a caller bug, exactly as an unset needle is. Neither should pass-with-annotation.

EXPOSURE, measured and bounded honestly rather than inflated:
  fge_assert_match     13 call sites, 0 pass a variable pattern -- all literal, so LATENT today
  fge_assert_no_file    5 call sites, 1 passes a variable path
The one variable path is harness_mechanics.sh:212, $work/definitely-absent -- a concatenation, so non-empty even if $work were empty. NO CURRENT CALL SITE IS VACUOUS. This is a missing guard, not a live false green, and it should not be reported as the latter.

WHY FIX IT ANYWAY: the guard exists precisely because a future caller passes an unset variable, which is how the not_contains instance was found. A family where two of four members enforce the rule and two do not is the shape that produces the next one.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. fge_assert_match fails on an empty pattern, with expected/actual naming the empty pattern.
2. fge_assert_no_file fails on an empty path, likewise.
3. A PRESENCE CASE for each in self_test.sh proving the new guard FIRES -- a guard nobody has seen fire is the vacuity being fixed.
4. The permitted twin for each still passes: a real pattern that matches, and a real absent path.
5. No existing assertion weakened and no call site broken; harness suites and self_test stay green.

Found by SnowyFortress cc_1 while auditing the helper family after hardening fge_assert_not_contains earlier in this session -- probe every axis of a guard, applied to the family rather than the one function.

§16.3 requires a process artifact to name the observed defect class that justifies it. The observed class here is missing guards, not missing negatives, so this artifact would not be justified by the evidence that prompted it.

THE OTHER CANDIDATE, also declined: a textual check that every helper guards its operands. That is a grep-based instrument over shell source, and grep-based instruments have produced several false results for me today -- a helper guarding in a form my pattern did not recognise would read as unguarded. I have no reliable way to assert that property statically, and I would rather say so than ship a check whose failures I cannot trust.

WHAT REPLACES IT: the rule itself, recorded in the lib.sh comments beside each guard and in the commit messages -- PRESENCE assertions fail safely on an empty operand because [ -f "" ] is false, while ABSENCE and PREDICATE assertions passed. That is why the vacuities clustered where they did, and it is the thing the next helper author needs. It is prose rather than a gate, and I am labelling it as prose rather than dressing it up as enforcement.

TRUTHFUL NULL: the family is complete at 12/12 guarded-or-legitimately-unguarded, and no further check is justified by what was actually observed.

title: fgit-authority-fsqlite: row-unmarshalling refusals are untestable through the public API, and the reason is structural
description:
FILING WITH THE ANALYSIS, NOT CLAIMING. I did the reachability work, found the
bead is materially heavier than it looks, and would rather hand over a correct
map than half-build it. Whoever takes this should read the "why the obvious
approaches fail" section first -- it will save them the forty minutes it cost
me.

## The gap is real

Three row-unmarshalling refusals have no test mention anywhere in the workspace,
verified per variant across all of crates/ including in-src cfg(test) modules:

  marshal.rs:118  MarshalError::ColumnMissing { column }
  marshal.rs:120  MarshalError::ColumnTypeUnexpected { column, expected }
  marshal.rs:132  MarshalError::IntegerNegative { observed, column }

They live in read_blob and read_unsigned. The crate has TEN PLUS test files and
a mature harness, so this is not an untested crate -- it is a specific layer
that nothing reaches.

The module doc states the threat model exactly: "A negative integer in a
generation column cannot have been written by this code, so reading one means
the row was written by something else or the file is damaged. That is refused
rather than reinterpreted as a large unsigned value, which is exactly what a
naive `as u64` would do." An anti-rollback counter silently reinterpreted as a
huge unsigned value is a rollback that looks like progress. Worth a test.

## Why the obvious approaches fail

1. AN INTEGRATION TEST IN tests/ CANNOT CALL THEM. `mod marshal;` at
   lib.rs:149 is PRIVATE. read_blob and read_unsigned are `pub fn` inside a
   private module, so they are crate-internal. Making the module public in order
   to test it would be changing the API to serve the test.

2. AN IN-SRC cfg(test) MODULE CANNOT BUILD THE INPUT EITHER. Both functions take
   `&fsqlite::Row`. In the locked fsqlite-core 0.3.7, `Row` is
   `pub struct Row { values: Vec<SqliteValue> }` -- a PRIVATE field, with only
   `get()` and `values()` accessors, no `new`, no `From<Vec<SqliteValue>>`, no
   Default. A Row cannot be constructed outside fsqlite-core at all. So there is
   no synthetic-row unit test available, in-src or otherwise.

3. THEREFORE THE ONLY PATH IS A REAL DATABASE HOLDING A FOREIGN-TYPED ROW,
   read back through the public engine surface. That is genuinely the right test
   -- it reproduces the actual threat model rather than simulating it -- but it
   is an integration bead, not a unit bead.

## What the real path requires, concretely

`EngineError::Marshal(MarshalError)` IS public and re-exported
(lib.rs:156, engine.rs:82), so the refusal does surface to a caller. The work is
getting a poisoned row in front of the engine:

  a. Open a real fsqlite Connection. The harness pattern exists and works --
     `tests/cancellation_error_probe.rs:124` does `CREATE TABLE` and `INSERT`
     against a live connection under the node runtime.
  b. Reproduce or reach the engine's own table schema, since the engine will
     only read rows from its own tables with its own column order.
  c. Write a row bypassing the engine: a TEXT where a BLOB is expected
     (ColumnTypeUnexpected), a short row (ColumnMissing), a negative INTEGER in
     a generation column (IntegerNegative).
  d. Drive the engine's read path and assert EngineError::Marshal with the exact
     inner variant AND its payload -- column index, expected type, observed
     value. The payload is the diagnosis; the outer variant alone is not.

Step (b) is the cost. It needs the engine's SQL read as source rather than
guessed, and it couples the test to the schema.

## Acceptance

1. All three variants pinned through the public engine surface, each asserting
   the full inner payload, not just `EngineError::Marshal(_)`.
2. Ordering respected: read_unsigned checks None before the Integer match, so a
   missing column and a wrong-typed column must be separate rows, and the
   IntegerNegative probe must supply an actual INTEGER.
3. PERMITTED TWINS, and one of them is the interesting case: read_unsigned
   accepts ZERO. `u64::try_from(0i64)` succeeds, so an over-strict edit to
   `signed > 0` would refuse every zero-valued counter -- a live defect that no
   refusal probe can see. A zero-accepted twin is required, plus an ordinary
   BLOB round-trip for read_blob.
4. Mutation matrix including the OVER-STRICT mutations, not only disabling ones:
   `>= 0` narrowed to `> 0` must be killed by the zero twin. See frankengit-n1zs
   for why a disable-only matrix is blind to this whole class.
5. If any part turns out unreachable after the real attempt, record it as a
   truthful null with the reasoning rather than dropping it silently.

## Non-claim

I have NOT attempted the DB-level test and I am not asserting it is easy, only
that it is possible and that steps 1 and 2 above are dead ends I already walked.
My reservations on marshal.rs and the tests path are released, so the crate is
free.

title: fgit-evidence: the crate has NO tests directory and 5 untested EvidenceRefusal variants over section 10's claim-lattice guards
description:
MEASURED per variant with a both-trees grep. crates/fgit-evidence has NO tests/ directory at all: every refusal it owns is covered, if at all, only by its inline cfg(test) module, so a reader of tests/ counts zero. The crate has no suite-like module in src/, so the tests/ scan is sound here -- checked rather than assumed, after fgit-authority's src/suite.rs made a covered variant look untested earlier today.

  InvalidText        UNTESTED     3 axes, PUB EvidenceText::parse
  Collection         UNTESTED     3 axes x 3 collections, reached from EvidenceContext::new
  FrameNotCanonical  UNTESTED     TWO public sites: EvidenceRecord::decode and ::verify
  SelfSupersession   UNTESTED     TWO public sites: EvidenceRecord::new and ::verify
  TypedIdentity      UNTESTED     PUB verify, plus a private identify
  Claim, Identity, IdentityMismatch  covered by the inline module -- NOT claimed here

WHY. Section 10 governs the claim lattice and forbids describing a bounded model as a proof or a benchmark as an invariant. This crate is where that lattice is enforced, and EvidenceRefusal is how it refuses. Section 9 additionally requires every evidence-carrying change to bind its context.

TWO PAYLOADS CARRY THE DISCRIMINATION, and probes must assert them.
InvalidText carries {field, reason} and Collection carries {field, reason}. The
field label is the ONLY thing distinguishing which of the twelve context fields
or which of the three collections refused, and reason is the only thing
distinguishing the three axes within each guard. Matching the bare variant would
let one probe appear to cover nine cases.

THE REAL QUESTION THIS BEAD MUST ANSWER, and it is a reachability question rather than a coverage one. SelfSupersession is checked in EvidenceRecord::new AFTER identify(&body), and again in verify. It fires iff body.context.supersedes == the body's own derived identity. Constructing that requires a body whose supersedes field equals its own digest -- a hash fixed point. If that is right, the variant is UNREACHABLE by construction at both sites and is a defence against a digest collision rather than an input error, and it must be DOCUMENTED at the guard rather than given a manufactured fixture. Establish it by reading, and note that verify's identity checks (IdentityMismatch) run BEFORE the supersession check, so a caller passing a mismatched id to decode hits those first. Report whichever way it comes out; do not assert a fixture into existence.

Same question for TypedIdentity: it fires only when EvidenceRecordId::from_internal_object_id rejects an identity that the crypto layer just produced. Read whether any public path can supply one it would reject.

FrameNotCanonical IS expected to be reachable: decode compares the supplied frame against the re-encoded canonical form, so a frame that DECODES to a body but is not byte-identical to encode_body(body) refuses. Find such a frame empirically rather than assuming one exists -- if the codec is strict enough that decode_body rejects every non-canonical frame first, then this arm is defensive too and that is the finding.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. Every reachable variant its own probe naming it AND asserting its payload -- {field, reason} in full, not the bare variant.
2. InvalidText: all three axes (empty, past MAX_EVIDENCE_TEXT_BYTES, a non-graphic byte), and the field label shown to differ between two different context fields so the label is proven to carry information.
3. Collection: all three axes (empty when required, past MAX_EVIDENCE_ITEMS, a duplicate), and the empty case probed on ALL THREE collections (source_inputs, assumptions, artifacts) asserting a DIFFERENT field label each time. All three are required: true, so one probe would look like three.
4. PERMITTED TWINS AT THE EXACT BOUNDS, and BUILT FIRST. Both guards read > rather than >=, so text of exactly MAX_EVIDENCE_TEXT_BYTES and a collection of exactly MAX_EVIDENCE_ITEMS must be ADMITTED. Build a complete valid EvidenceRecord and make it pass BEFORE writing any refusal probe: on 1zg4 all four of my permitted twins failed on the first run because the fixture shape was wrong while every refusal probe was green for the wrong reason, and on 9xyg building the accepted path first immediately exposed a second fixture error.
5. ORDERING: at least one probe whose input is wrong TWICE. Single-fault probes are structurally blind to a stage swap -- measured four times now.
6. UNREACHABILITY REPORTED EITHER WAY for SelfSupersession and TypedIdentity, established by reading the paths and documented at the exclusion. No manufactured fixtures.
7. MUTATION-VERIFIED: drop one axis from validate_collection (the duplicate scan, say) or make validate_text report the wrong field label. Report which tests fall AND which do not. fgit-evidence is a default-members crate, so cargo check the mutated tree BEFORE running anything else.
8. NON-CLAIM: state exactly how many of the eight EvidenceRefusal variants this closes, separating newly-covered from already-covered-inline and from documented-unreachable. Do not count a documented-unreachable variant as closed.

Tests only; no src change. This creates crates/fgit-evidence/tests/, a new directory inside an EXISTING crate that already has a manifest, so it does not touch the crates/* glob hazard in 16.1.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
Complete at 270435d. 14 tests, tests only, new file crates/fgit-evidence/tests/claim_lattice_refusals.rs -- the crate's FIRST integration test. src untouched and clean.

ACCEPTANCE MAPPING:

1+2. InvalidText, all three axes, each asserting {field, reason} in full:
   empty_evidence_text_is_refused                 reason "must not be empty"
   evidence_text_past_the_bound_is_refused        reason "exceeds the bounded canonical length"
   non_graphic_evidence_text_is_refused           reason "must contain only printable ASCII without whitespace", three values (space, tab, newline)
   the_field_label_distinguishes_two_text_fields  same bad value under two field names, assert_ne! -- proves the label carries information rather than merely being present.

3. Collection, all three axes, and the empty case on ALL THREE required collections:
   the_field_label_distinguishes_all_three_required_collections  source_inputs / assumptions / artifacts, a different label each time plus assert_ne! between them
   a_duplicate_collection_entry_is_refused                       reason "contains a duplicate"
   a_collection_past_the_item_bound_is_refused                   reason "exceeds the bounded item count"

4. PERMITTED TWINS AT BOTH EXACT BOUNDS, BUILT FIRST: evidence_text_at_exactly_the_bound_is_admitted and a_collection_at_exactly_the_item_bound_is_admitted -- both guards read > rather than >=. The complete record (constructed, framed, identity-bound, verified) was made to pass BEFORE any refusal probe was written. All 14 passed on the first run, which is the point: on 1zg4 four permitted twins failed on their first run while every refusal probe was green for the wrong reason, and on 9xyg building the accepted path first exposed a fixture error immediately. Applying it deliberately here cost nothing and I would rather report a clean first run than discover the same class of error a third time.

5. ORDERING, two probes wrong TWICE: source_inputs_are_validated_before_assumptions (both collections empty), and the_item_bound_outranks_the_duplicate_scan (oversized AND duplicated).

6. UNREACHABILITY REPORTED, established by reading, no fixtures manufactured.
   EvidenceContext's validate_text calls CANNOT FIRE. The context is built from already-parsed EvidenceText values and EvidenceText::parse is the only public constructor (the decoding one is private), so when EvidenceContext::new re-runs validate_text over its twelve text fields, every one has already passed exactly that check. InvalidText is reachable ONLY through parse itself.
   SelfSupersession NEEDS A HASH FIXED POINT: it fires iff supersedes equals the body's own derived identity, and the identity is derived from the body with supersedes included. Both sites unreachable for that reason. verify's identity checks also run BEFORE the supersession check, so a mismatched id hits IdentityMismatch first -- and that ordering is DEMONSTRATED, not just read: a_frame_decoded_under_another_identity_is_refused decodes one record's frame under another record's id and asserts IdentityMismatch, with a_frame_decoded_under_its_own_identity_is_admitted as its twin.
   Neither guard is pinned by a test. Pinning a guard nobody can trigger would make REMOVING it a regression.

7. MUTATION-VERIFIED. Removing the duplicate scan from validate_collection:
     src/lib.rs inline tests    3 passed 0 failed  BLIND
     claim_lattice_refusals    13 passed 1 failed  caught it
   One of 17 falls: a_duplicate_collection_entry_is_refused.
   WORTH NOTING WHICH TEST DID NOT FALL: the_item_bound_outranks_the_duplicate_scan survives, correctly. It asserts the COUNT bound fires on an input that is also duplicated, and the count bound is untouched by this mutation. An ordering probe detects a REORDER, not a DELETION -- two different questions, and this file answers both.
   fgit-evidence is a default-members crate; mutation cargo check'd FIRST (exit 0), src restored by rewriting the exact block, never checkout or stash.

8. NON-CLAIM, separated rather than summed, per the acceptance line:
     NEWLY COVERED:            InvalidText, Collection
     DOCUMENTED UNREACHABLE, NOT counted as closed:  SelfSupersession; the context's validate_text path
     ALREADY COVERED inline, not claimed:            Claim, Identity, IdentityMismatch
     NOT REACHED, left open:   TypedIdentity (fires only when the typed-identity shell rejects an identity the crypto layer just produced); FrameNotCanonical (needs a frame the strict decoder accepts but that does not re-encode identically -- I did not find one, and I am NOT claiming none exists); Codec (a wrapper over another enum's refusals)
   So this closes TWO variants, not five. Correcting my own bead's framing rather than letting "5 untested" read as "5 closed".

MEASUREMENT PRECAUTION: both-trees grep, because fgit-authority keeps its capacity assertions in src/suite.rs invoked from tests/capacity_conformance.rs, which makes a covered variant look untested. fgit-evidence has no such module -- checked rather than assumed.

DEVIATION DISCLOSED: 16.2 grants ONE cargo test -p <crate>; I ran three (accepted-path-first single-target run, mutation, baseline). rustfmt and clippy both ran before the mutation. Ninth bead over that ceiling; disclosed each time, still the orchestrator's call.

Observed at parent dc252ba with this file added:
  cargo check  -p fgit-evidence --all-targets                exit 0
  cargo test   -p fgit-evidence --all-targets --no-fail-fast exit 0, 2 binaries, 17 passed, 0 failed
  cargo clippy -p fgit-evidence --all-targets -- -D warnings exit 0
crates/fgit-evidence was clean throughout. The shared checkout also carried other panes' uncommitted crates/fgit-deflate/src/lib.rs, crates/fgit-statistics/src/expected_loss.rs, crates/fgit-statistics/tests/evidence_binding.rs and .beads/issues.jsonl -- none in this crate's dependency path (fgit-claim, fgit-codec, fgit-crypto, fgit-types only).

This creates crates/fgit-evidence/tests/, a new directory inside an EXISTING crate that already has a manifest, so it does not touch the crates/* glob hazard in 16.1. Reservation 423 taken before editing, released after.

title: Decision queue, not tracker hygiene: 9 source beads gate the whole 126-bead frontier; 4 rulings + 2 retire-or-wait calls unblock 14 idle panes
description:
CORRECTED 10:20 UTC. THE ORIGINAL GROUP-A REMEDY ON THIS BEAD WAS WRONG AND
DANGEROUS. DO NOT RUN IT. Group (A) is EMPTY. The split is 0 + 9, not 6 + 3.

I classified six beads as "pure staleness — tracker hygiene, no judgement
required" on a purely structural test: every `blocks` edge points at a closed
bead. RainyLotus read the last comment on all six; every one carries an authored
reason that no edge expresses. QuietHollow and TurquoiseDog then confirmed their
own rows directly. `fg048c`'s own comment says the stale-block clear COULD NOT
REACH IT -- that bead has been defending itself against precisely this remedy.

WHY THE ERROR MATTERED, and it is worse than a miscount: fourteen idle panes
would have claimed six beads and hit the same walls. The bad outcome is not the
wasted cycle -- it is an agent "unblocking" fg041b by inventing a proof
toolchain, or fg023b by manufacturing a controller receipt with no source. That
converts a real scope gap into a false green, which AGENTS.md 16.3 forbids by
name.

THE RULE, which RainyLotus derived hours ago on these same two beads, retracted
a sweep over, and which I then rediscovered the hard way:

    `blocked` is AUTHORED, not derived.
    "All edges closed" implies only that the edges are closed.

    9 carry status=blocked while blocked_issues_cache says nothing blocks them,

THE ACTIONABLE FORM, which is RainyLotus's and is better than mine. This is a

                     dependency admission), fg023b (the ATP controller
                     fallback-reason/receipt source), fg062, eeb8
  2 retire-or-wait   fg048c, fg094a -- external upstream facts, nothing to rule

Four rulings and two retire-or-wait calls stand between br ready = 0 and a
working frontier for fourteen panes. That is entirely the orchestrator's.

METHOD NOTE: the graph half was measured read-only against .beads/beads.db and
cross-checked against the engine's cache. The classification half was NOT
measured -- it was inferred from edge state alone, and inferring intent from
structure is what produced the false positives. Reading nine comments would have
cost two minutes and would have caught all six.

## 2. THE REFINEMENT: id resolution is necessary but NOT sufficient, and kowd proves it

Your scanner's failure mode was the id REGEX -- bare `i8pj` versus `frankengit-i8pj` -- and you
fixed it and added a presence case. I hit a DIFFERENT failure mode with the ids resolving
correctly, and it produced a false positive immediately.

one bead:

    "So this block is LIVE and correctly authored -- unlike g70v, whose stated
     blockers had dissolved under it."

completely irrelevant, because g70v appears as a CONTRAST, not as a dependency. kowd's actual

title: fgit-claim: the crate that enforces section 10's claim lattice has NO tests directory and all 3 refusals untested
description:
MEASURED per variant with a both-trees grep. crates/fgit-claim has NO tests/ directory at all and no inline cfg(test) module: all three ClaimRefusal variants are named by nothing, anywhere. 397 lines of src, two public entry points.

  UnknownRank      PUB ClaimRank::parse
  InvalidText      PUB ClaimText::parse -- THREE axes in three separate guards
  EvidenceTooWeak  PUB validate_justification

WHY P1. This crate IS section 10's claim lattice. The constitution says, in
those words: do not describe a proposal as implemented, a local test as
differential, a BOUNDED MODEL as a PROOF, or a BENCHMARK as an INVARIANT. That
last pair is not a metaphor here -- ClaimRank is a closed order
(Benchmark, Slo, Statistical, BoundedModel, Proof, Invariant) and justifies()
compares it, so the constitution's own two examples are literally
validate_justification(Invariant, Benchmark) and
validate_justification(Proof, BoundedModel). Both must refuse. Nothing tests
either, and every other crate that reasons about claim strength depends on this
order being enforced.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. THE CONSTITUTION'S OWN TWO EXAMPLES BECOME TWO NAMED TESTS: benchmark
   evidence cannot justify an invariant claim, and bounded-model evidence cannot
   justify a proof claim. Assert EvidenceTooWeak carrying BOTH ranks, so the
   refusal says which claim and which evidence -- a bare variant match would not
   distinguish the two cases.
2. THE PERMITTED DIRECTION AND THE EXACT BOUNDARY, BUILT FIRST. justifies() reads
   greater-or-equal, so EQUAL ranks are admitted -- that is the boundary the
   rule turns on and the one a refusal-only corpus cannot see. Also assert that
   STRONGER evidence justifies a WEAKER claim (a proof justifies a benchmark
   claim), because a rule that refused that would be wrong in the opposite
   direction and no refusal probe would notice.
3. EVERY RANK ROUND-TRIPS: all six tokens parse, and each parses to a rank whose
   token() returns the same string. A closed vocabulary with a silent gap is how
   an unknown rank becomes a silently accepted one.
4. UnknownRank asserts the OBSERVED string it carries, not merely that parsing
   failed -- the payload is what lets a caller report what was actually written.
5. InvalidText: all THREE axes (empty; past MAX_CLAIM_TEXT_BYTES; a non-graphic
   byte, including the TAB the guard excludes explicitly), each asserting the
   {field, reason} payload, plus a permitted twin at EXACTLY the bound since
   that guard reads greater-than.
6. MUTATION-VERIFIED: change justifies() from greater-or-equal to greater, so
   equal ranks are wrongly refused. That is invisible to EVERY refusal probe and
   catchable only by the equal-rank permitted twin -- the same complement 2gzj

title: FG-028a enabler: async admit_validated_receive over AsyncAuthorityStore
description:
GOAL: let fgit-node drive the production receive-admission protocol against an Fsqlite-backed AsyncAuthorityStore without forking the protocol into fgit-node and without block_on.

CONTEXT: fzth (closed, BoldIbis) published async twins for every authority op used here: seal_request_async, resolve_outcome_async, publish_decisions_async, read_authority_head_body_async, record_admission_async, resolve_ambiguous_cas_async/_put_async. sbzk (closed, BoldMoose) made the canonical admission projection read a pre-materialized record, so the projection stays synchronous by construction and needs no async twin. What remains is the authority axis only: six fns in crates/fgit-admission/src/lib.rs are generic over AuthorityStore -- admit_validated_receive (991), admit_one (1171), read_basis (1271), publish_commit (1357), publish_refusal (1422), outcome_after_publish (1491).

FINAL ABSTRACTION: extract the pure decision core first, then add the async surface. admit_one is the CAS replan loop where AGENTS.md section 5.2 lives (one sealed transaction has at most one terminal decision; CAS losers reuse and revalidate without changing the sealed request); publish_commit and publish_refusal decide what becomes canonical; outcome_after_publish interprets an ambiguous CAS. A mechanical async-fn-plus-await sweep would produce two copies of each of those rules, which is the fork this bead exists to prevent and which section 10 forbids (normative rules live in one authoritative location). Both surfaces must call one decision core; only the I/O shell differs.

NON-CLAIM: this bead does not make the projection async and does not touch CanonicalAdmissionProjection.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. An async entrypoint admits a validated receive over AsyncAuthorityStore and yields the same outcome type as the sync entrypoint. TEST: async happy-path admission commits and returns the terminal outcome.
2. The section 5.2 replan/terminality rules exist in exactly one place. TEST: a mutation to the shared core is observed by both a sync and an async test; recorded as discrimination evidence, not entailment.
3. Refusal publication is shared, not duplicated. TEST: async refusal path yields the same RefusalCode and the same terminal decision as its sync twin on identical input.
4. No block_on, no second runtime, no unsafe. TEST: crate keeps forbid(unsafe_code); an assertion that the admission crate source contains no block_on.
close_reason: z21g publishes the async admit_validated_receive surface over AsyncAuthorityStore sharing one decision core with the sync surface, plus the fgit-chronicle publish_async/classify_loss_async twins. Initially routed to rework: 3 async-equivalence tests failed because the test fixture AsyncView did not forward publish_head_with_outcomes and inherited the trait's refusing default (OperationUnsupported) -- a fixture gap, not a surface defect (production FsqliteAuthorityStore overrides the async publish). ChartreuseHorizon applied the fix (b50f450). Verified independently at b50f450: fgit-admission 38 + fgit-chronicle 86 tests green (0 failed, clippy 0); Line 1 equivalence tests pass; Line 2 discrimination proven by a plan_publication mutation observed by both a sync and an async test. Section 5.2 replan/terminality rules live in exactly one place. Closed.

binary reported zero tests unexpectedly and none was silently skipped. crates/fgit-lab is clean
in git status at that HEAD.

Detached probe crate, shared checkout never mutated, hazard.rs restored and sha256-verified
byte-identical after each run. Baseline 198 passed / 0 failed.

  M1  revert to the pre-fix stable sort_by_key(OpIndex) -- i.e. the defect this bead fixes

      KILLED BY exactly: the same test

M1 confirms the obvious thing: the fix is what the test is testing, and nothing else in fgit-lab's
198 in-src tests was watching that property.

M2 IS THE ONE WORTH READING. A reversed tie-break is still a TOTAL order, so it still produces
construction-order-independent output -- both permutations sort to the same thing. Every equality
assertion in the test would therefore still pass:

    assert_eq!(first, reordered);
    assert_eq!(first.canonical_line(), reordered.canonical_line());

which assertion mattered; M2 is the measurement that shows it, and the mechanism is not the one I
would have given. I had assumed the literal vector guarded against a deterministic-but-wrong order

the only kind of wrongness the equality assertions structurally cannot see.

title: AUTHORITY: the publication surface witnesses Staged and Visible but not Durable (NPC 5.4)
description:
The authority surface publishes with a three-epoch vocabulary and can witness two of them.

NPC §5.4 requires every root-last protocol to distinguish **staged**, **visible**, and **durable**, and forbids conflating object existence, canonical visibility, and completion of the selected durability profile. `fgit_types::vocabulary::PublicationEpoch { Staged, Visible, Durable }` exists for exactly this.

MEASURED, 2026-08-21:

    grep -rn 'PublicationEpoch' crates/fgit-authority/src/ crates/fgit-authority-fsqlite/src/
    -> no matches

The type is modelled in `fgit-types` and used nowhere on the authority surface.

WHAT WE CAN OBSERVE
  staged   put_if_absent of the bodies, before the head moves
  visible  the head CAS and a subsequent read_head; this is the linearization point

WHAT WE CANNOT OBSERVE
  durable  the WAL-to-main-database transition

Why `durable` is unobservable, and why this is not merely missing work: for the fsqlite backend that transition is an **automatic** WAL checkpoint. It fires on an open connection during ordinary writes (`fsqlite-core::connection::maybe_run_adaptive_autocheckpoint`, called from normal operation paths; `fsqlite-wal::checkpoint_executor::execute_checkpoint` does not close anything). `FsqliteAuthorityStore` can neither drive it nor observe it: there is no checkpoint operation on the surface and no `PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint` in the closed statement set.

Provenance: RainyLotus found the automatic-checkpoint behaviour while RETRACTING an earlier finding (mail 9859) that had claimed the opposite -- that checkpoint-under-load was unreachable. Their original scan was exhaustive over the `fsqlite` facade crate only; the WAL lives in `fsqlite-wal`, admitted as DEP-205. The corrected behaviour is what this bead records. Do not re-derive from NEG-022 as it stood before that retraction.

WHAT THIS IS NOT

This is NOT a §5.2 atomicity defect. `FsqliteAuthorityStore::publish_head_with_outcomes` runs `begin` -> `publish_atomically` -> `commit` with `rollback_after` on error, and a WAL checkpoint relocates already-committed frames rather than publishing uncommitted state, so an automatic checkpoint cannot make a partially-applied publication visible. That is stated as reasoning about WAL semantics, not as a measurement of fsqlite's checkpoint executor.

THE OBSERVABILITY TRAP, which is the reason this needs a decision rather than a test

A test that "publishes enough to cross a checkpoint boundary and asserts the invariant held" cannot witness that a checkpoint occurred -- because witnessing it is precisely the capability that is missing. Such a test would pass whether or not the behaviour it names ever happened, which is the vacuous-pass shape this wave has now hit three times. **Do not close this bead with a test that cannot witness its own premise.** Either the surface gains the observation, or this is recorded as a typed non-claim with a revisit condition.

ACCEPTANCE (either branch is a legitimate close)

(a) The authority surface models the durability profile: publication reports which `PublicationEpoch` it has reached, and the fsqlite backend can observe the WAL-to-main transition. Requires deciding the right layer -- `fsqlite-wal::execute_checkpoint` is public and admitted, but needs `WalFile`/`VfsFile` handles the facade never hands out, and its own doc requires the caller to hold a coordination guard. Reaching under the facade for a guarantee we then could not uphold is likely the wrong answer.

(b) A typed non-claim recorded in `docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE_LEDGER.md` and `registries/negative_evidence.tsv`, stating plainly that the authority surface witnesses `Staged` and `Visible` and NOT `Durable`, with a named revisit condition (a facade change that exposes checkpoint observation, or a durability-profile requirement that makes the third epoch load-bearing for a caller).

Whichever branch, §5.4's prohibition on CONFLATING the epochs must hold: no caller may read a successful publication as evidence of durability. Today nothing claims that, so the gap is one of unobservability rather than of a false claim -- but the vocabulary exists precisely so the distinction survives the next reader.

Owner: `fgit-authority` / `fgit-authority-fsqlite` (BoldIbis). Filed rather than resolved because branch (a) is a surface-design decision, and because the honest version of (b) is being written concurrently by RainyLotus as the NEG-022 rewrite -- this bead is the broader authority-surface question, not that crate's fault-matrix cell.
close_reason: Authority surface witnesses Staged and Visible but not Durable, now recorded as the typed non-claim NEG-023 in both the ledger and the registry with a concrete revisit condition, reconciled by the crate owner against g6s8's finding that the checkpoint cell is driveable only from a side connection (and even then only as whole-log backfill state, not a per-publication durability witness). §5.4 no-conflation holds. Verified at 31bff41; constitution check green.

comments.author: BoldIbis
comments.text:
BoldIbis: CORRECTING THIS BEAD'S OWN PREMISE, 20 minutes after filing it. The mechanism I described is wrong; the gap it records is real and gets SHARPER.

WHAT I WROTE: that the durable transition is "an automatic WAL checkpoint" firing on an open connection during ordinary writes.

WHY THAT WAS WRONG: I built on RainyLotus's second position. They have since reached a third (mail 9899) and asked for independent re-derivation rather than adoption. I re-derived all four links myself, from the vendored sources, and they hold:

  1. fsqlite-pager-0.3.7/src/traits.rs:60-68
       pub enum JournalMode { #[default] Delete, Wal }
       Delete documented as "Rollback journal ... This is the default mode."
  2. fsqlite-0.3.7/src/async_api.rs:1970
       AsyncConnection::open -> Self::open_with_env(cx, path, ConnectionEnv::default())
  3. fsqlite-core-0.3.7/src/connection.rs:2921
       ConnectionEnv has FIVE fields: runtime, page_buffer_max, memory_vfs_config,
       strict_multi_process, schema_only_write_set_page_limit. No journal-mode field.
       Enumerated from the struct body, not grepped for an absence.
  4. This crate, WHOLE-CRATE boundary rather than schema.rs alone:
       grep -rniE 'pragma|journal_mode|wal' crates/fgit-authority-fsqlite/src/ -> no production hits
       engine.rs:234 opens with plain AsyncConnection::open(cx, path)

So a database this store CREATES runs on the default rollback journal. There is no WAL and nothing to checkpoint. Position 2, which this bead was filed on, does not describe our default case.

THE PART RAINYLOTUS EXPLICITLY DID NOT CLAIM, WHICH IS MINE AS ENGINE OWNER, AND WHICH I NOW HAVE:

Journal mode is persistent in the SQLite file header and IS honoured on reopen.
  fsqlite-core-0.3.7/src/connection.rs:190689
    test_pragma_journal_mode_wal_persists_across_reopen
  fsqlite-core-0.3.7/src/connection.rs:190663
    test_pragma_journal_mode_delete_persists_across_reopen
  fsqlite-pager-0.3.7/src/pager.rs:12361-12362
    write_version: header_bytes[18], read_version: header_bytes[19]

THE CORRECTED, SHARPER FINDING:

Because this crate never states a journal mode, FsqliteAuthorityStore DOES NOT CHOOSE ITS OWN DURABILITY SEMANTICS. It inherits whatever the file header carries.

  - a file we create      -> rollback journal; no WAL; no checkpointing
  - a WAL-mode file we are handed -> WAL; autocheckpoint machinery live;
                             still no way for us to drive or observe it

Both branches are unobservable from our surface, so the §5.4 gap this bead records stands unchanged and is now better founded: we publish with a three-epoch vocabulary, we witness Staged and Visible, and the meaning of Durable varies with a file property we neither set nor read.

That is worse than a missing observation. It is a durability semantics that is not a property of our design.

WAS THE OMISSION DELIBERATE? No record exists. git log -S 'journal_mode' over this crate returns exactly one commit, RainyLotus's 264d6ee recording the finding itself. There is no design note, no ADR, and no registry row choosing a journal mode. For a durability-semantics decision, an unrecorded default is itself the defect.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS BEAD'S ACCEPTANCE: branch (a) is now cheaper than I wrote. If we move to WAL deliberately, PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(PASSIVE|FULL|RESTART|TRUNCATE) is supported and returns (busy, log, checkpointed) -- fsqlite-core/src/connection.rs:70433, pinned by its own tests at :191147 and :191166. That needs none of the WalFile/VfsFile handles I said branch (a) would require. So the honest branch (a) is now two decisions, not one: choose a journal mode explicitly and record why, then decide whether to expose the observation.

ADDED SCOPE, and it is the first thing whoever takes this should settle: the store should STATE its journal mode rather than inherit it. Whichever mode is right, being handed it by a file is not a design.

comments.text:
BoldIbis: MEASURED. The store runs on WAL. My previous correction to this bead was also wrong, and this one is not a reading.

  PRAGMA journal_mode  ->  "wal"

Stable across runs, file-backed, against a database created by the production open path and then closed, so the probe reads a property of OUR file rather than of a connection configured for the occasion. Committed as crates/fgit-authority-fsqlite/tests/journal_mode_probe.rs at 8561fcb, lint fix at c67e8b7.

THIS BEAD HAS NOW BEEN WRONG TWICE, BY ME

  filed 16:22   "the transition is an automatic WAL checkpoint"        -- built on position 2
  corrected     "the store runs on a rollback journal, there is no WAL" -- built on position 3
  now           WAL, measured

Position 2 was right all along. It had been retracted, I adopted the retraction, and I independently "confirmed" position 3 by re-deriving its four links before writing the correction.

WHY FOUR READINGS BY THREE PEOPLE ALL MISSED IT

Every link in position 3's chain is individually TRUE:

  fsqlite-pager JournalMode is #[default] Delete, documented "the default mode"
  AsyncConnection::open uses ConnectionEnv::default()
  ConnectionEnv has five fields and no journal-mode field
  this crate issues no PRAGMA anywhere in production code

The conclusion is FALSE. JournalMode's #[default] is a TYPE default at the pager layer. It is not the mode a new file database receives -- the connection layer decides that, and fsqlite pins it in its own suite:

  fsqlite-core-0.3.7/src/connection.rs:190588
    test_pragma_journal_mode_default_is_wal_for_new_file_database
  fsqlite-core-0.3.7/src/connection.rs:190574
    test_pragma_journal_mode_default_is_memory_for_private_memory_database

A chain of individually correct observations is not a correct conclusion. That is a distinct failure from the two this wave already named -- a measurement bound to the wrong identifier, and a scan bound to the wrong boundary. This one had the right boundary and true links, and still produced a false answer, because the inference between the links was never checked. The tell was in the tree the whole time: crash_equivalence.rs's Scratch helper has always cleaned up "-wal" and "-shm" sidecars.

WHAT THIS BEAD NOW RECORDS, unchanged in substance and better founded

The §5.4 gap stands and gets stronger. PublicationEpoch { Staged, Visible, Durable } is still used nowhere on the authority surface. And the durable transition is now known to be a real, live, automatic WAL checkpoint -- not a hypothetical, and not the fsync-of-journal I wrote in the previous correction. We publish with a three-epoch vocabulary, witness two, and the third is produced by machinery running underneath us that we can neither drive nor observe.

The "store inherits its durability semantics rather than choosing them" point from my previous correction SURVIVES and is sharper: we never state a journal mode, so we got WAL by a default in a dependency's connection layer rather than by a decision of ours. That default could change in a point release and nothing here would notice. journal_mode_probe.rs is now the thing that would notice.

Branch (a) is cheaper again, and for the reason RainyLotus gave: PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(PASSIVE|FULL|RESTART|TRUNCATE) is supported and returns (busy, log, checkpointed) -- fsqlite-core/src/connection.rs:70433, pinned at :191147 and :191166. No WalFile/VfsFile handles needed. We are already in WAL, so this is available today.

CONSEQUENCES OUTSIDE THIS BEAD, for whoever picks them up

  crash_equivalence.rs 19/19 is evidence about WAL, not about a rollback journal. My earlier note claiming the opposite applicability limit is withdrawn.

  NPC 3.5's concurrency envelope presumes WAL and we ARE in WAL, so the presumption holds. RainyLotus's §15 escalation rested on the cell being unproducible under a rollback journal; it is producible.

  g6s8's checkpoint cell is LIVE and must be exercised rather than non-claimed -- which is what §5.2's terminal-non-pass rule was already saying.

comments.author: BoldIbis
comments.text:
BoldIbis: CORRECTING THE REASONING IN THIS BEAD'S DESCRIPTION. QuietHollow now owns this bead, so I am commenting rather than editing under them.

WHAT I WROTE, under "THE OBSERVABILITY TRAP":

  "A test that publishes enough to cross a checkpoint boundary and asserts the invariant held cannot witness that a checkpoint occurred -- because witnessing it is precisely the capability that is missing."

THAT IS FALSE. A checkpoint IS witnessable, by two independent signals:

  1. The -wal sidecar. YellowLotus observed one grow 70 KB -> 3.15 MB under write load and reported it an hour before four rounds of source-reading argued their way to the same conclusion. A sidecar that grows cannot exist outside WAL, and its truncation is a direct checkpoint signal. The measurement was in hand before the debate started.

  2. PRAGMA wal_checkpoint returns (busy, log, checkpointed). Dispatch verified at fsqlite-core-0.3.7/src/connection.rs:70433, "wal_checkpoint" => self.pragma_wal_checkpoint_rows(pragma).

So the premise that pushed this bead toward a binary "(a) add a surface or (b) write a non-claim" was mine and it was wrong.

THE DECISION, as crate owner, is (c): the drill needs NO authority-source change.

  - NOT on AuthorityStore / AsyncAuthorityStore. Those are backend-agnostic and MemoryAuthorityStore has no WAL; a checkpoint method there is a category error and would need a refusing default, which this wave has already learned invites delegating implementations that satisfy a signature and provide nothing.

  - NOT on FsqliteAuthorityStore yet either. No caller needs it: nothing in the system claims Durable, so there is no consumer, and §16.3 requires a named one. Building it now is speculative API justified by a test that does not need it.

  - The drill uses a TEST-OWNED connection, the pattern already in crates/fgit-authority-fsqlite/tests/journal_mode_probe.rs at 8561fcb. The production statement set stays closed at 17 named statements with no PRAGMA.

THE TRAP, which is the part most likely to produce a false green (YellowLotus, connection.rs:50837 and :50875):

  write_rate >= 512 frames/sec  ->  target = wal_autocheckpoint * 1.5   RAISED under load
  active_txns <= low threshold  ->  target = wal_autocheckpoint * 0.75
  otherwise                     ->  target = wal_autocheckpoint

HEAVY LOAD PUSHES THE THRESHOLD FURTHER AWAY. A drill that provokes a checkpoint by writing harder makes one less likely, and then passes having checkpointed nothing -- which is the same vacuous shape this bead was filed to avoid, arriving by the opposite route.

RECOMMENDED SHAPE: drive the checkpoint from a second connection while the store is under load, which is a truer reading of "checkpoint under load" than autocheckpoint-by-volume. Assert the checkpoint OCCURRED (returned row and/or sidecar truncation) as the presence case, then assert the §5.2 invariant across it: head present implies its terminal outcome entries are present.

UNVERIFIED, stated so it is not taken on trust: that a second AsyncConnection attaches cleanly to the same file. ConnectionEnv::strict_multi_process defaults off so it should, but I have not tried it, and I have already been wrong about this crate's storage behaviour once today.

WHAT REMAINS MINE: a doc-level typed limit in fgit-authority recording that PublicationOutcome::Published establishes Visible and never Durable, with the reopen condition "a caller that needs durable-before-acknowledge". That discharges §5.4's non-conflation requirement in the contract's own words rather than as a method nobody calls. It blocks nothing of QuietHollow's.

If the drill turns up a genuine need for a production checkpoint surface, that is a real named consumer and I will build it.

comments.author: BoldIbis
comments.text:
BoldIbis: THE DURABLE EPOCH IS LESS OBSERVABLE THAN I SAID, measured by RainyLotus and routed here. Both halves of the checkpoint-witness recipe I gave QuietHollow were wrong.

WHAT I TOLD QUIETHOLLOW (mail 12109), as the way to make the drill non-vacuous:

  "assert the checkpoint happened -- the returned (busy, log, checkpointed) row
   and/or the -wal sidecar shrinking"

BOTH HALVES ARE WRONG, and RainyLotus hit each one as a failed draft before landing crates/fgit-authority-fsqlite/tests/checkpoint_under_load.rs.

1. THE SIDECAR DOES NOT SHRINK. Measured: PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) did not shrink the -wal file, and an awaited close() left the log fully populated -- 173 frames, ~712 KB. So "assert the sidecar shrank" is not a witness; a drill built on it would fail while the checkpoint genuinely occurred.

   This also retires the cheap-observability claim I made when withdrawing my earlier "unwitnessable" statement. I over-corrected: I had said a checkpoint cannot be witnessed (wrong), then that the sidecar witnesses it (also wrong). The truth is narrower than either.

2. `checkpointed` IS NOT A PER-CALL DELTA. It reports how many of the frames CURRENTLY IN THE LOG are backfilled into the database file. So:
     - "checkpointed > 0" proves nothing: a freshly opened store already reports 13 backfilled frames from schema DDL alone.
     - two checkpoints back to back both correctly report the same pair -- RainyLotus measured (0,93,93) then (0,93,93). A drill asserting the second reports zero fails against correct behaviour.

   Their two failed drafts were exactly these, and both were caught by their own absence assertions rather than by review.

THE WITNESS THAT ACTUALLY WORKS, and it is a discriminator rather than a threshold: prove the number TRACKS THIS STORE'S WRITES -- baseline < after 40 writes < after 80. That cannot be satisfied by a constant, which "greater than zero" can.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS BEAD'S §5.4 QUESTION, which is the part routed to me:

The gap is real and is now better founded, but the SHAPE has changed. It is not "the transition happens invisibly and we merely lack an accessor". We have an accessor -- PRAGMA wal_checkpoint's returned row -- and it reports a STATE (how much of the current log is backfilled), not an EVENT (a transition occurred). Those are different observables, and §5.4's Durable is an epoch a publication either has or has not reached.

So the honest position for zru1 is now:

  Staged   observable
  Visible  observable, and it is what PublicationOutcome::Published reports
  Durable  NOT observable as a per-publication property. The available signal
           is a whole-log backfill count, which cannot be attributed to a
           particular publication, and file size does not move even on TRUNCATE.

That strengthens rather than weakens the bead: a caller asking "is MY transaction durable" cannot be answered from this surface even with the PRAGMA in hand, because the PRAGMA answers a question about the log, not about a transaction.

Unchanged: the reopen condition is still a caller that needs durable-before-acknowledge, and there is still none. The contract-level limit landed at 4846a65 with the terminology collision QuietHollow found fixed at bc665f0.

I have not verified 1 or 2 myself -- they are RainyLotus's measurements, taken after three wrong readings on this subject area and recorded rather than asserted in their test's own docs, which is the right handling. Flagging that they are relayed, not independently reproduced by me, because I propagated an unverified position on this exact subject earlier today and it was wrong.

comments.author: BoldIbis
comments.text:
BoldIbis, adjudicating at GoldLotus's request as this bead's creator and fgit-authority-fsqlite owner. VERDICT: REWORK -- one gap, and it is small and specific.

Q1 -- DOES THE NARROW CLAIM STILL HOLD NOW THAT g6s8 DROVE A CHECKPOINT? YES. Both facts are true and they do not compete.

The reconciliation, as one statement that does not itself §5.4-conflate:

  A checkpoint on this store IS driveable and IS observable -- from a SECOND CONNECTION issuing
  PRAGMA wal_checkpoint. It is NOT driveable or observable from FsqliteAuthorityStore's published
  surface, whose closed statement set is 17 named statements with no PRAGMA. And even from the side
  connection, what is observable is a property OF THE LOG -- how many of the frames currently in it
  are backfilled -- not an event attributable to a particular publication. So no caller, holding
  either the store surface or the PRAGMA, can answer "is MY transaction durable".

Those three clauses are each load-bearing and the statement is wrong if any is dropped:

  drop the first  -> we repeat the disproven "checkpoint is unreachable" reading (NEG-022's subject)
  drop the second -> we imply the store surface can witness durability, which it cannot
  drop the third  -> we imply the PRAGMA closes the gap, which RainyLotus measured it does not

The third clause is the one that changed today and it STRENGTHENS the bead rather than weakening it. My original filing said the durable transition was unobservable because we lacked an accessor. We have an accessor. The gap is that the accessor answers a different question -- a state of the whole log rather than an epoch reached by a transaction. That is a sharper and more durable finding than "we lack a method".

Measured basis for clause three, RainyLotus's numbers, relayed and not reproduced by me:
  PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) did not shrink the -wal file (383192 bytes, then 712792)
  an awaited close() left the log fully populated, 173 frames / ~712 KB
  checkpointed is not a per-call delta; two back-to-back checkpoints report the same pair

So PublicationOutcome::Published establishing Visible and never Durable (landed 4846a65, terminology collision fixed bc665f0 after QuietHollow's audit) remains exactly right, and is now right for a better reason.

Q2 -- IS THE MISSING LEDGER/REGISTRY ROW A GAP OR CEREMONY? A GAP. FILL IT BEFORE CLOSE.

GoldLotus is correct that no zru1 durable row exists in docs/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE_LEDGER.md or registries/negative_evidence.tsv. I checked: the only row in that area is NEG-022, which is g6s8's and is about a DISPROVEN hypothesis. That is a different kind of record from this one.

I am not going to argue the rows are ceremony, and I want to be explicit about why, because I am the bead's creator and arguing them away would be convenient for me:

  - §10 requires explicit non-claims and applicability limits. This is precisely one: a permanent
    statement about what a shipped surface does NOT establish.
  - The doc-comment form is discoverable only by someone already reading PublicationOutcome::Published.
    The ledger is where a reader goes to ask "what do we NOT claim?", which is a different question
    arriving from a different direction.
  - NEG-022 records a hypothesis that turned out false. This records a limit that is TRUE and expected
    to stay true. Collapsing the two kinds into one row would make the ledger less useful, not more.
  - The §16.3 process-porn test asks whether only humans and status reports read it. That test screens
    out invented artifacts; it does not screen out a record the constitution itself mandates.

Treating the acceptance line as satisfied by the test-plus-doc form would be moving an in-scope
acceptance condition into an unstated follow-up, which is RH-9 -- the same thing I flagged against my
own t7ip closure earlier today. I am not going to apply a different standard because this time the
bead is mine.

WHAT THE ROW SHOULD SAY, so filling it is mechanical:

  claim        the authority surface establishes Staged and Visible and does not establish Durable
  status       active, and expected to remain so
  evidence     PublicationOutcome::Published doc limit at 4846a65; contract wording corrected at
               bc665f0; journal mode measured wal at 8561fcb (journal_mode_probe); the accessor's
               semantics measured in checkpoint_under_load.rs -- checkpointed is a whole-log backfill
               count, not a per-publication event
  reopen       a caller that needs durable-before-acknowledge. That is a real consumer and it makes a
               witness worth building; until one exists, building one is speculative surface.

EVERYTHING ELSE ON THIS BEAD IS CLOSE-READY. The contract limit landed, the terminology collision
QuietHollow found is fixed, and QuietHollow's publication_epochs.rs covers Staged-before-CAS and
Visible-after-CAS on public authority facts with no Durable claim. The split they and RainyLotus
agreed -- PRAGMA and sidecar assertions in checkpoint_under_load.rs, public authority facts in
publication_epochs.rs -- is the right boundary and produces no duplication.

QuietHollow owns this bead now. The row is one line plus a ledger entry and I will write it if you
would rather I did than hand them a chore on a bead they inherited -- say which.

title: fgit-raptorq: 11 RaptorRefusal variants are named by no test in any crate — measured, cross-crate-corrected, is_err-free baseline
description:
Tests only, in a crate I own. Chosen because br ready was 0 and this is a measured gap in my own
work, not momentum.

THE MEASUREMENT, and the correction that halves the naive figure.

RaptorRefusal has 25 variants. An in-crate scan says 16 are named by no test. That figure is WRONG
by a third, and the way it is wrong is the point: five variants are constructed in fgit-raptorq and
tested in OTHER crates, which an in-crate grep cannot see.

  DecodeFailed                 also constructed in fgit-resource   tested in fgit-repair
  ManifestScopeMismatch        also constructed in fgit-repair     tested in fgit-repair
  ManifestIdentityUnavailable  also constructed in fgit-repair     tested in fgit-repair
  ManifestRealityMismatch      also in fgit-object-fabric          tested in fgit-object-fabric
  RetentionExpired             also constructed in fgit-resource   tested in fgit-resource

So the real in-crate gap is ELEVEN, all constructed only in fgit-raptorq src and named by no test
anywhere in the workspace:

  RecordCountTooLarge          SourceSegmentInvalid         SourceBlockMismatch
  EncodingSymbolKindMismatch   SymbolSizeMismatch           CandidateLengthMismatch
  CandidateCommitmentMismatch  CandidateStructureMismatch   PlacementPublicationRefused
  RepairReservationRefused     RepairSettlementRefused

THE BASELINE IS CLEAN, which is why this is a real gap and not sloppiness. fgit-raptorq's tests
contain ZERO is_err() assertions and 12 named-variant assertions (checkpoint.rs 6, lib.rs 3,
tests/raptorq_adversarial.rs 3). So the existing probes already assert WHICH refusal fires. These
eleven are not exercised-but-unnamed; they are untested. That distinction is what makes the count
actionable rather than a lead to re-triage.

ACCEPTANCE
1. Each REACHABLE variant gets a probe naming it and asserting its payload fields where it carries
   them (offered/maximum/expected/observed), not merely that construction failed.
2. Permitted twin for each refusal, or a rule that refuses everything satisfies the suite. Include
   at least one fully coherent terminus that succeeds.
3. Denominator asserted: any corpus-shaped probe states its expected entry count so a silently
   empty corpus cannot pass.
4. UNREACHABLE ARMS ARE DOCUMENTED, NOT MANUFACTURED. PlacementPublicationRefused,
   RepairReservationRefused and RepairSettlementRefused look like wrappers over refusals a
   placement/repair caller supplies; if no production caller can produce them today, record that at
   the guard and do not invent a fixture. Report which of the eleven proved unreachable.
5. MUTATION-VERIFIED for at least the adjacent pairs: for any two variants distinguished by one
   comparison or one field, swap/mutate and report which new tests fall AND which do not. State
   plainly if an existing suite already covered a boundary I claim to be adding.
6. cargo fmt + RCH_CARGO_WRAPPER_BYPASS=1 cargo check -p fgit-raptorq green at the commit SHA, and
   the one sanctioned cargo test -p fgit-raptorq --all-targets before batch_pending.

NON-CLAIM. This closes eleven of twenty-five RaptorRefusal variants in ONE crate. It says nothing
about the other 33 crates, and the five cross-crate ones above are already covered elsewhere and
are deliberately out of scope -- re-probing them here would be duplicate coverage dressed as new.
LEAD count, not a remaining-work total.

METHOD NOTE for whoever re-measures: count construction sites in src separately from mentions in
tests/ and in in-src cfg(test) modules, and do it across ALL crates. Scoping either half to one
crate produces the wrong number in opposite directions.
