comments.author: CloudyTiger
comments.text:
SCOPE SPLIT after reading every construction site. The 11 is right as a MEASUREMENT and wrong as a
work item for this crate. Narrowing before writing code, with the reasons.

1. NOT REACHABLE -- DOCUMENT, DO NOT MANUFACTURE (AC 4)
   RecordCountTooLarge (lib.rs:86) is u32::try_from(reader.len()) on a slice length. Reaching it
   needs more than u32::MAX records in one segment. Defensive; it gets a comment at the guard and
   no fixture.

2. BELONGS TO fgit-repair, NOT HERE -- and building it here would duplicate a peer's harness
   RepairReservationRefused (lib.rs:561), RepairSettlementRefused (596 and 616 -- TWO sites),
   PlacementPublicationRefused (602) all live inside repair_microsegment, whose only production
   caller in the tree is crates/fgit-repair/src/lib.rs:795. Reaching them means driving the whole
   happy path and then failing one injected port. fgit-repair ALREADY has that harness:
   tests/scrub_scheduler.rs implements RepairPlacementAuthority twice (ScriptedSource :170,
   CancellingSource :217). Re-creating ScriptedSource inside fgit-raptorq to reach three variants
   would be duplicate machinery, and fgit-repair is not my crate. These three are a lead FOR THAT
   CRATE'S OWNER, not work for this bead. Not filing it for them -- naming it so the count is not
   silently absorbed here.

3. MINE, AND THE REAL WORK. Two near-identical ordered guard chains, one per profile:
     checkpoint.rs 470-490   accept path for CheckpointRaptorProfile
     lib.rs        654-674   accept path for MicrosegmentRaptorProfile
   Same five guards in the same order (ScopeMismatch, EngineObjectIdMismatch, SourceBlockMismatch,
   EncodingSymbolKindMismatch, SymbolSizeMismatch); the first two are already covered, the last
   three are not, at EITHER site. Plus the candidate-validation pair at checkpoint.rs:444/447 and
   lib.rs:462/468 (CandidateLengthMismatch, CandidateCommitmentMismatch), CandidateStructureMismatch
   (lib.rs:465, 574), and SourceSegmentInvalid (lib.rs:381, reachable by handing
   protect_microsegment malformed bytes).

TWO STRUCTURAL FACTS THAT CHANGE HOW THIS IS WRITTEN.

  (a) THE PROBES MUST BE IN-SRC, NOT IN tests/. I reserved
      crates/fgit-raptorq/tests/refusal_coverage.rs and will not use it. ScopedCheckpointSymbol has
      PRIVATE FIELDS AND NO PUBLIC CONSTRUCTOR -- the existing corpus builds malformed symbols with
      struct-literal syntax only because it sits in an in-src cfg(test) module (the crate's own
      comment at checkpoint.rs:689 says exactly this). An integration test cannot construct a
      malformed symbol at all. So these land in the cfg(test) modules of checkpoint.rs and lib.rs.

  (b) THE TWO SITES ARE INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM THEIR REFUSALS, INCLUDING PAYLOAD. I expected
      SymbolSizeMismatch{expected} to tell the checkpoint site from the microsegment site. It does
      not: CheckpointRaptorProfile::SYMBOL_BYTES = 128 and MicrosegmentRaptorProfile::SYMBOL_BYTES
      = 128, and MAX_SOURCE_BYTES is 8*1024 in both. So the ONLY discriminator is which entry point
      the test calls. Each of the three shared variants therefore needs a probe per chain, and that
      must be stated in the test names -- otherwise a future divergence in one profile is covered
      by a test that only ever exercised the other.

REVISED COUNT FOR THIS BEAD: 7 variants across 2 chains, 1 documented-unreachable, 3 routed to
fgit-repair. I will report the mutation results per AC 5 against that set, and I will not describe
the routed three as closed by anything I do here.

comments.text: PROGRESS: 175c4c3 (microsegment twins + SourceSegmentInvalid, 187 insertions) and 45a5787 (unreachability documented at both CandidateLengthMismatch guards, 10 insertions, comment-only). With 1b71402 that is 5 of the 7 in-scope variants resolved: SourceBlockMismatch, EncodingSymbolKindMismatch and SymbolSizeMismatch probed on BOTH chains; SourceSegmentInvalid probed through protect_microsegment with a fully succeeding permitted twin; CandidateLengthMismatch shown DEFENSIVE rather than untested and documented at both sites. comments.author: CloudyTiger
comments.text:
ENGINE-LEVEL READING of the two open Candidate* variants. No code this cycle. Three of the four
links are now settled by reading asupersync-0.4.9 -- the version Cargo.lock actually resolves,
which I checked after first opening 0.2.9 from the registry by mistake -- and the one that remains
is named precisely, so the sanctioned test run settles it in one shot rather than by experiment.

LINK 1, AUTHENTICATION -- CLOSED.
security/context.rs:253 sign_symbol_tag computes AuthenticationTag::compute(&self.key, symbol)
over the symbol CONTENT. A forgery signed with the same SecurityContext the decoder was built with
therefore authenticates, so AuthenticationRejected cannot pre-empt the candidate checks.

LINK 2, LENGTH -- CLOSED, AND IT CONFIRMS 45a5787 AT THE ENGINE LEVEL.
decoding.rs:973 into_data concatenates the decoded blocks and then clips the result to
object_size via Vec's shortening method. object_size is the second ObjectParams field, which is
exactly expected.source_len() -- the same value CandidateLengthMismatch compares against. That
operation can only shorten, never lengthen, so under consistent parameters the length matches by
construction.

My committed comment argued this from symmetry between the two call sites. It is now verified
inside the engine, and the phrase "only an engine violating its own parameter contract" turns out
to be literally right: a short output would require a decoded block shorter than its own plan.

LINK 3, COMPLETION CRITERION -- CLOSED.
decoding.rs:919 is_complete is completed_blocks.len() == plans.len(), i.e. block-based.
sum_required_symbols (with repair_overhead 1.0) feeds only the InsufficientSymbols error text and
progress(), so a full source set is not disqualified by an overhead threshold.

LINK 4, STILL OPEN, and it is the whole remaining question.
Whether feeding k forged source symbols causes the inactivation decoder to MARK THE BLOCK DECODED.
  - If it does: the candidate is source_len bytes of attacker-chosen data, its digest differs from
    the scope's commitment, and CandidateCommitmentMismatch fires. Reachable. The microsegment
    chain would reach CandidateStructureMismatch the same way, through MicrosegmentReader::open
    failing on non-segment bytes.
  - If it does not: the run yields DecodeFailed and the probe is simply wrong.
That is a property of InactivationDecoder, and I will not predict it.

NOT SHIPPING A PROBE ON THREE QUARTERS OF AN ARGUMENT. The obvious dodge -- asserting
"CandidateCommitmentMismatch OR DecodeFailed" -- is a weakened assertion that passes either way
and proves nothing, which is worse than leaving the gap visible. These two stay open until a run
answers link 4, and the sanctioned pre-batch_pending test is exactly the run that would.

comments.text: PROGRESS at b55d3a9 (124 insertions across both chains, test-only). Closes a gap in MY OWN earlier probes, found by re-reading 1b71402 and 175c4c3 rather than by anything failing. The kind guard is a DISAGREEMENT test -- id.is_source(k) != kind().is_source() -- so it has two directions, and both earlier probes covered only one: a repair-kind symbol in a source slot. An implementation checking only 'a repair symbol must not claim a source slot' would have passed both and left the other direction unguarded. One axis found is not the guard characterised. b55d3a9 adds the reverse on both chains: a SOURCE-kind symbol in a REPAIR slot. asupersync 0.4.9 defines SymbolId::is_source(source_count) as esi < source_count (types/symbol.rs:185-187), so esi == source_symbols is the FIRST repair slot and the exact boundary where the id stops claiming to be a source symbol -- the probe sits on that boundary rather than deep in the repair range, because the boundary is where an off-by-one in the comparison would surface. Each is paired with a permitted twin at the same boundary slot with the kind corrected, so the pair isolates the disagreement rather than the kind. Reachability is by construction: earlier guards satisfied deliberately (scope cloned from a real protect_* result, object id from that scope, sbn 0) and the size guard sits AFTER the kind guard, so a full-size payload reaches it. cargo check -p fgit-raptorq --all-targets and rustfmt clean at b55d3a9; tests still unrun, bead still in_progress. Variant count unchanged at 5 of 7 -- this deepens coverage of a variant already claimed rather than adding a new one, and I am not counting it as progress against the acceptance list.

comments.text: PROGRESS at 2388024 (73 insertions, both chains, test-only). Second application of the b55d3a9 review, to a different guard of mine. The size guard is scoped.symbol.len() != expected_size -- an INEQUALITY, so two directions, and 1b71402/175c4c3 probed only the short one. A guard written 'len < expected_size' would have passed everything I had shipped while admitting an oversized symbol, i.e. trailing bytes the decoder was never told about. 2388024 adds the over direction on both chains and asserts the payload with it, which also witnesses that 'offered' carries the ACTUAL length rather than a clamped or saturated value on that side. title: fgit-git-object: the commit/tag header refusals are unnamed, and the profile pair that makes them Git-compatible is untested in both directions
description:
Chosen by measuring refusal coverage across all 34 crates, then verifying the gap is real rather than a name-grep artifact, then choosing on subject matter.

MEASUREMENT, stated precisely because the two obvious ways to count disagree:
  ObjectError has 34 variants, all constructed in src.
  Unnamed by ANY test:            16
  Unnamed by INTEGRATION tests:   34   (the other 18 are named only inside in-src cfg(test) modules)
The honest figure is 16. Anyone reading tests/ alone would conclude 34, which is why this is written
down. None of the 16 is even MENTIONED bare in any test file, so they are genuinely untested rather
than exercised-without-being-named.

WHY THIS CRATE. Section 6 requires preserving native Git object identity exactly and states that
resource limits and refusal behaviour ARE compatibility semantics. These are the refusals that decide
whether a commit or tag is well formed.

THE PROPERTY THAT MAKES THIS MORE THAN COVERAGE. parse_commit and parse_tag take an
AcceptanceProfile, and validate_strict_commit / validate_strict_tag run ONLY under StrictCreate. The
enum documents the intent: StrictCreate rejects malformed or non-canonical structures BEFORE
FrankenGit creates them; GitCompatibleImport preserves historically tolerated structures with a
bounded unambiguous parse.

So every strict refusal has a built-in permitted twin -- the SAME BYTES under the import profile --
and that pair is the actual Git-compatibility obligation. Testing only the refusal half leaves the
half that matters unpinned: if the import profile wrongly refuses, FrankenGit cannot read real
repositories; if the strict profile wrongly accepts, FrankenGit creates objects Git would consider
malformed. Neither direction is currently covered.

SCOPE, the header-structure cluster, all reachable through parse_commit and parse_tag with plain
bytes:
  parse_headers, profile-independent:
    a header line with no space separator     -> MalformedHeader
    a header line with an empty name          -> MalformedHeader   (second axis, same variant)
    a continuation line with no preceding header -> OrphanHeaderContinuation
  parse_headers, StrictCreate only:
    a header name outside [a-z0-9-]           -> InvalidStrictHeaderName
  validate_strict_commit, StrictCreate only:
    no headers at all                         -> MissingOrDuplicateCommitTree
    two author headers, or none with a later author/committer -> MissingOrDuplicateCommitIdentity
  validate_strict_tag, StrictCreate only:
    missing or duplicated tag header          -> MissingOrDuplicateTagHeader
    a tag name that is not admissible         -> InvalidTagName

ACCEPTANCE:
1. Each refusal has a probe NAMING the variant, asserting payload fields where the variant carries
   them.
2. MalformedHeader is probed on BOTH axes -- no separator and empty name -- since one variant covers
   two conditions and a probe hitting one leaves the other unexercised.
3. THE PROFILE PAIR, which is the point of the bead: every StrictCreate-only refusal is paired with
   the SAME BYTES parsed under GitCompatibleImport, asserted to SUCCEED. That is what proves the
   refusal is a creation policy rather than a parse failure, and it is the half that keeps FrankenGit
   able to read real repositories.
4. The profile-INDEPENDENT refusals are shown to refuse under BOTH profiles, so the pair in 3 is
   attributable to policy rather than to the import profile accepting everything.
5. ORDERING: parse_headers runs before validate_strict_*, so a probe for a validation refusal must
   supply headers that lex cleanly. State what each probe passes through, and include a permitted
   terminus -- a well-formed commit and tag parse under both profiles.
6. MUTATION-VERIFIED: make one StrictCreate-only guard fire under both profiles and report which
   tests fall AND which do not, plus whether the existing corpus already covers it. That corpus
   includes an adversarial_refusal.rs, so the answer may well be partial coverage; state whichever it
   is, as on 33ib and dw7i where the honest answer was that a fixture already protected the boundary.
7. REACHABILITY: AllocationFailure and DecoderStateInconsistent are excluded from this bead --
   try_reserve failure and an internal invariant, both likely defensive. If any scoped arm proves
   unreachable, document it at the guard rather than manufacturing a fixture.
8. NON-CLAIM: this closes 7 of the 16 genuinely-unnamed ObjectError variants. The loose-header and
   tree-entry clusters remain, and the 18 covered only by in-src modules are a separate question.
   LEAD count, not a remaining-work total.

Tests only; no src change. fgit-git-object is clean and unreserved; I hold no standing there, so this
is an independent-adversary corpus over a crate I do not own. Blast radius note: it is a
default-members crate, so any mutation probe must cargo check the mutated tree BEFORE running
anything else.
